cases.requirement: The `exists` operator reports SUPPORTED when the addressed field carries a non-empty value
cases.risk: If `exists` cannot recognise a value that is plainly there, every workflow built on it reports a false failure and the customer stops trusting the product
cases.setup: Assertion `{operator:'exists', field:'record.correlation_id', expected:''}` against CrmRecordEvidence whose correlation_value is 'enq-1001'
cases.expected: evaluateAssertions returns status SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED and observed_display 'enq-1001'

cases.requirement: A missing correlation value yields the distinct CORRELATION_MISSING reason, not the generic VALUE_MISMATCH
cases.risk: Correlation is the one setup step customers get wrong; a generic mismatch message sends them hunting the wrong problem
cases.setup: `exists` on record.correlation_id, CRM evidence present but correlation_value is the empty string
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code CORRELATION_MISSING

cases.requirement: Boundary: a whitespace-only value does not satisfy `exists`
cases.risk: A CRM property containing a single space is an empty property; treating it as present would manufacture a VERIFIED out of nothing
cases.setup: `exists` on record.property 'verify_ref' whose observed value is '   '
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code VALUE_MISMATCH

cases.requirement: Boundary: `exists` against a property the provider never returned is CONTRADICTED, because `exists` is evaluated before the undefined guard
cases.risk: This is the one operator where undefined means 'not there' rather than 'we could not see'; getting it backwards turns a real absence into an unknown and delays the customer's answer
cases.setup: `exists` on record.property 'verify_ref' where the properties map has no such key at all
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code VALUE_MISMATCH, not UNKNOWN/EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE

cases.requirement: `equals` reports SUPPORTED on an exact string match of a named CRM property
cases.risk: The most common rule in the product; a wrong answer here is a wrong answer everywhere
cases.setup: `equals` on record.property 'lead_source' with expected 'website_form' and the same observed value
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: `equals` reports CONTRADICTED when the provider returned a different value
cases.risk: This is the defect class the product exists to catch: the automation wrote the wrong value and its own log said success
cases.setup: `equals` on record.property 'lead_source' expecting 'website_form', observed 'import'
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code VALUE_MISMATCH and observed_display 'import'

cases.requirement: Boundary: `equals` against a field the provider omitted entirely is UNKNOWN, never CONTRADICTED
cases.risk: Calling a field we could not see 'wrong' is a false FAILED, which is as damaging as a false VERIFIED for a monitoring product
cases.setup: `equals` on record.property 'lead_source' where the properties map does not contain that key (value undefined)
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE

cases.requirement: Boundary: `equals` against a field the provider returned as null is CONTRADICTED — an authoritative empty
cases.risk: The null/undefined distinction is the whole contradicted-versus-unknown boundary; collapsing them loses either real failures or honest unknowns
cases.setup: `equals` on record.property 'lead_source' where the properties map contains the key with value null
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code VALUE_MISMATCH

cases.requirement: `equals` is case-sensitive for non-email fields
cases.risk: Silently widening an equivalence class is how a false VERIFIED is made; 'Acme Ltd' and 'acme ltd' are different property values
cases.setup: `equals` on record.property 'company' expecting 'Acme Ltd', observed 'acme ltd'
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code VALUE_MISMATCH

cases.requirement: `equals` trims surrounding whitespace on both the expected and observed values before comparing
cases.risk: CRM exports routinely carry trailing spaces; failing a run for an invisible character would train customers to ignore failures
cases.setup: `equals` on record.property 'company' expecting 'Acme Ltd', observed ' Acme Ltd '
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: `equals` on record.email is case-insensitive — the documented exception to case-sensitive comparison
cases.risk: Mailbox case is not significant at any production provider; treating it as significant produces false failures on real customer data
cases.setup: `equals` on record.email expecting 'ann@example.com', observed 'Ann@Example.com'
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: `not_equals` reports SUPPORTED when the observed value differs from the forbidden one
cases.risk: Used to assert a record did not land in a default or placeholder state; a broken negative check hides exactly the misrouting it was written for
cases.setup: `not_equals` on record.property 'lifecycle_stage' forbidding 'subscriber', observed 'lead'
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: `not_equals` reports CONTRADICTED when the observed value is the forbidden one
cases.risk: Without this the rule is decorative and the customer believes a check is running that never fires
cases.setup: `not_equals` on record.property 'lifecycle_stage' forbidding 'subscriber', observed 'subscriber'
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code VALUE_MISMATCH

cases.requirement: `not_equals` against an authoritative empty is UNKNOWN, not SUPPORTED — success is never inferred from absence
cases.risk: An absent value trivially 'is not X'; letting that pass would make every negative assertion self-satisfying and produce false VERIFIED runs
cases.setup: `not_equals` on record.property 'lifecycle_stage' forbidding 'subscriber', observed null
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE

cases.requirement: `not_equals` against a field the provider omitted is UNKNOWN with EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE
cases.risk: Same false-pass risk as the null case, reached by a different code path (the undefined guard rather than the operator body)
cases.setup: `not_equals` on record.property 'lifecycle_stage' where the key is absent from the properties map
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE

cases.requirement: `normalised_email_equals` lowercases both addresses before comparing
cases.risk: Resend and HubSpot disagree on address casing in their payloads; a case difference must never be reported as the wrong recipient
cases.setup: `normalised_email_equals` on message.recipient expecting 'ann@example.com', observed 'ANN@EXAMPLE.COM'
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: `normalised_email_equals` reduces a `Display Name <addr@host>` form to the bare address
cases.risk: Email providers return the RFC 5322 display form; comparing it literally would fail every run where the automation set a display name
cases.setup: `normalised_email_equals` on message.recipient expecting 'ann@example.com', observed 'Ann Smith <ann@example.com>'
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: `normalised_email_equals` removes a single trailing dot on the domain (the DNS root)
cases.risk: Fully-qualified domains with the root dot appear in some provider payloads and are the same mailbox
cases.setup: `normalised_email_equals` on message.recipient expecting 'ann@example.com', observed 'ann@example.com.'
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: Documented boundary: `+tag` is NOT stripped, so a tagged address does not satisfy an assertion about the untagged mailbox
cases.risk: Stripping the tag would let a customer satisfy 'we emailed the enquirer' with an address they control themselves — a deliberate route to a false VERIFIED
cases.setup: `normalised_email_equals` on message.recipient expecting 'boss@corp.com', observed 'boss+verify@corp.com'
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code VALUE_MISMATCH

cases.requirement: Documented boundary: dots in the local part are NOT removed, because that equivalence is Gmail-specific
cases.risk: Applying a single provider's addressing quirk globally would widen the equivalence class on every other mail host and mask a genuinely wrong recipient
cases.setup: `normalised_email_equals` on message.recipient expecting 'ann.smith@example.com', observed 'annsmith@example.com'
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code VALUE_MISMATCH

cases.requirement: `normalised_email_equals` strips surrounding double quotes left by a provider's own escaping
cases.risk: A quoted address is the same mailbox; failing on the quoting would produce a false failure the customer cannot act on
cases.setup: `normalised_email_equals` on message.recipient expecting 'ann@example.com', observed '"ann@example.com"'
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: A value with no '@' falls back to a whole-string lowercase comparison rather than throwing
cases.risk: A malformed recipient in a provider payload must produce a verdict, not an exception that kills the whole observation
cases.setup: `normalised_email_equals` on message.recipient expecting 'ann@example.com', observed 'undisclosed-recipients'
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code VALUE_MISMATCH and no exception is thrown

cases.requirement: `one_of` reports SUPPORTED when the observed value is a member of the allowed set
cases.risk: Customers use this for lifecycle stages that legitimately have several acceptable values; a broken set check forces them to write brittle equals rules
cases.setup: `one_of` on record.property 'lifecycle_stage' allowing ['lead','marketingqualifiedlead'], observed 'lead'
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: `one_of` reports CONTRADICTED when the observed value is outside the allowed set
cases.risk: This catches an automation writing a record into an unexpected stage — a silent misrouting the platform's own log never reports
cases.setup: `one_of` on record.property 'lifecycle_stage' allowing ['lead','marketingqualifiedlead'], observed 'customer'
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code VALUE_MISMATCH

cases.requirement: `one_of` against record.email applies the email case-insensitivity rule to each member of the set
cases.risk: Inconsistency between operators on the same field would make the rule language unpredictable and the docs untrue
cases.setup: `one_of` on record.email allowing ['ann@example.com','ops@example.com'], observed 'ANN@example.com'
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: A `one_of` rule with an empty allowed array is refused as an unusable spec
cases.risk: An empty set can never be satisfied; answering CONTRADICTED would report a customer configuration mistake as an automation failure
cases.setup: `one_of` on record.property 'lifecycle_stage' with expected []
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code RULE_UNSUPPORTED and no comparison is attempted

cases.requirement: Boundary: `occurred_within` is inclusive at exactly N seconds
cases.risk: An exclusive bound would fail a run that landed precisely on the agreed window, and the boundary is the value customers set deliberately
cases.setup: `occurred_within` 300 on message.occurred_at, evidence timestamp exactly 300000ms after the source event's occurred_at
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: Boundary: `occurred_within` fails one millisecond past the window
cases.risk: The pair with the inclusive case proves the comparison is a real bound rather than an approximate one
cases.setup: `occurred_within` 300 on message.occurred_at, evidence timestamp 300001ms after occurred_at
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code OUTSIDE_TIME_WINDOW

cases.requirement: Evidence that predates the business event contradicts `occurred_within` rather than satisfying it
cases.risk: A pre-existing CRM record matched by correlation would otherwise prove an enquiry the automation never actually handled
cases.setup: `occurred_within` 600 on record.created_at, record created 60 seconds before the source event's occurred_at
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code OUTSIDE_TIME_WINDOW

cases.requirement: Boundary: a delta of exactly zero satisfies `occurred_within`
cases.risk: Same-instant timestamps are common when a provider stamps the event from the same clock; rejecting them would be an off-by-one against real data
cases.setup: `occurred_within` 600 on record.created_at, record created_at identical to the source event's occurred_at
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: An unparseable timestamp is UNKNOWN, not late
cases.risk: A corrupt provider timestamp is a gap in our evidence, not a proven breach of the customer's deadline; reporting it as FAILED would be a lie about their automation
cases.setup: `occurred_within` 600 on message.occurred_at with the observed value 'not-a-date'
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE

cases.requirement: A negative `occurred_within` window is refused as an unusable spec
cases.risk: A negative window is meaningless; evaluating it would produce arbitrary verdicts from a configuration mistake
cases.setup: `occurred_within` -1 on message.occurred_at with a valid timestamp present
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code RULE_UNSUPPORTED

cases.requirement: `provider_status_in` reports SUPPORTED when any observed event carries an allowed status
cases.risk: The delivery assertion is the second half of the product's only workflow; missing a genuine 'delivered' would report a working automation as broken
cases.setup: `provider_status_in` on message.status allowing ['delivered'], events ladder ['accepted','delivered']
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: A delivery-proving rule contradicted by a bounce is CONTRADICTED, not unknown
cases.risk: A bounce is definitive evidence the acknowledgement never reached the enquirer — the exact failure the customer bought this to catch
cases.setup: `provider_status_in` allowing ['delivered'], events ladder ['accepted','bounced']
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code STATUS_NOT_REACHED

cases.requirement: 'accepted' alone never satisfies a delivery-proving rule; the answer is UNKNOWN because a 'delivered' event may still arrive
cases.risk: Conflating 'the sending service took it' with 'the mail server received it' is the single most tempting false VERIFIED in the email half of the product
cases.setup: `provider_status_in` allowing ['delivered'], events ladder ['queued','accepted'], deadline still open
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code STATUS_NOT_REACHED

cases.requirement: An 'opened' event never satisfies a delivery-proving rule on its own
cases.risk: Open tracking is a pixel, not a delivery receipt, and the product publicly claims it never treats an open as proof anyone read anything
cases.setup: `provider_status_in` allowing ['delivered'], events ladder ['opened']
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code STATUS_NOT_REACHED

cases.requirement: A hard failure event contradicts a non-delivery status rule too
cases.risk: A customer whose rule only asks for 'accepted' still needs to be told when the send definitively failed, rather than being left at unknown
cases.setup: `provider_status_in` allowing ['accepted'], events ladder ['failed']
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code STATUS_NOT_REACHED

cases.requirement: Explicit allowed-set membership wins over the delivery-contradiction heuristic
cases.risk: A customer verifying that a complaint was recorded must not have their own rule overruled by a general-purpose failure heuristic
cases.setup: `provider_status_in` allowing ['complained'], events ladder ['delivered','complained']
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: `provider_status_in` addressed at a field other than message.status is refused
cases.risk: The operator reads the whole status ladder; pointing it at a recipient or an id would compare incomparable things and produce a meaningless verdict
cases.setup: `provider_status_in` on message.recipient allowing ['delivered']
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code RULE_UNSUPPORTED

cases.requirement: A status literal outside the EMAIL_STATUS vocabulary is refused rather than silently never matching
cases.risk: A typo like 'send' would otherwise produce a permanently unknown rule that looks like a provider problem instead of a configuration one
cases.setup: `provider_status_in` on message.status allowing ['send']
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code RULE_UNSUPPORTED

cases.requirement: observed_display for a status ladder lists every observed status, not only the chosen one
cases.risk: The report has to show the customer the whole sequence, otherwise 'we saw accepted but not delivered' is unexplainable
cases.setup: `provider_status_in` allowing ['delivered'], events ladder ['queued','accepted','deferred']
cases.expected: observed_display contains all three statuses in observation order

cases.requirement: SUPPORTED outranks CONTRADICTED when several email events address the same single-value rule
cases.risk: A later corrective event must be able to rescue a run; ranking the wrong way round would report a resolved problem as a permanent failure
cases.setup: `equals` on message.recipient with two events, the first carrying a wrong recipient and the second the expected one
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED, and evidence_ref points at the matching event

cases.requirement: CONTRADICTED outranks UNKNOWN when several candidates address the same rule
cases.risk: Definite bad news must never be buried under a missing field from a different event
cases.setup: `equals` on message.recipient with one event whose recipient is absent and one whose recipient is wrong
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code VALUE_MISMATCH

cases.requirement: An AMBIGUOUS_MATCH gap makes every assertion on that source UNKNOWN even when a record is present in the bundle
cases.risk: If we cannot tell which of two CRM records is the customer's, nothing derived from either is trustworthy, and guessing is how a false VERIFIED is made
cases.setup: CRM evidence present plus a gap {source:'crm_record', code:'AMBIGUOUS_MATCH'}
cases.expected: Every crm_record assertion is UNKNOWN with reason_code RECORD_AMBIGUOUS and no operator runs

cases.requirement: A NOT_FOUND gap on crm_record with no candidates maps to RECORD_NOT_FOUND
cases.risk: This is the reason code that later licenses a FAILED at the deadline; mapping it to a generic unavailability would make genuine absence unprovable
cases.setup: Empty bundle with a gap {source:'crm_record', code:'NOT_FOUND', retryable:false}
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code RECORD_NOT_FOUND

cases.requirement: A NOT_FOUND gap on email_event maps to the distinct EVENT_NOT_OBSERVED reason
cases.risk: Customers need to know which half of the workflow is missing; one shared reason code would make the report useless for diagnosis
cases.setup: Empty bundle with a gap {source:'email_event', code:'NOT_FOUND', retryable:false}
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code EVENT_NOT_OBSERVED

cases.requirement: An AUTH_EXPIRED gap maps to CONNECTION_UNAVAILABLE, which is an access problem and never an automation failure
cases.risk: Reporting our own expired token as the customer's broken automation would destroy the product's credibility on first contact
cases.setup: Empty bundle with a gap {source:'crm_record', code:'AUTH_EXPIRED', retryable:false}
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code CONNECTION_UNAVAILABLE

cases.requirement: A PERMISSION_MISSING gap also maps to CONNECTION_UNAVAILABLE rather than to a missing record
cases.risk: A revoked scope looks exactly like an empty CRM from the connector's point of view; conflating them would blame the customer for our access problem
cases.setup: Empty bundle with a gap {source:'crm_record', code:'PERMISSION_MISSING', retryable:false}
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code CONNECTION_UNAVAILABLE

cases.requirement: A RATE_LIMITED gap maps to EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE, a retryable condition distinct from a broken connection
cases.risk: The scheduler branches on this distinction; mislabelling a rate limit as terminal would abandon runs that would have resolved on the next attempt
cases.setup: Empty bundle with a gap {source:'email_event', code:'RATE_LIMITED', retryable:true}
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE

cases.requirement: An empty bundle with no gap at all is AWAITING_EVIDENCE — the evaluator never claims the connector established absence
cases.risk: AWAITING_EVIDENCE is deliberately not in the authoritative-absence set, so this path can never become a FAILED at the deadline
cases.setup: Bundle with crm null, no email events and an empty gaps array
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code AWAITING_EVIDENCE

cases.requirement: A record living in a different provider account contradicts the assertion with RECORD_WRONG_ACCOUNT
cases.risk: A customer-supplied record id is a locator, never a fact; evidence from another tenant's HubSpot account must never support a verification
cases.setup: CRM evidence whose provider_account_id is 'hub-999' while the workspace's connected account is 'hub-001'
cases.expected: Result is CONTRADICTED with reason_code RECORD_WRONG_ACCOUNT

cases.requirement: When candidates are mixed, foreign-account evidence is dropped and the owned record is evaluated normally
cases.risk: Dropping the whole bundle on a single foreign event would lose real evidence; keeping the foreign event would import another account's data
cases.setup: Two email events for the same message id, one from account 'res-999' and one from the connected 'res-001' carrying status delivered
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED and evidence_ref names the event from account res-001

cases.requirement: The account gate is skipped when the workspace's connected account id is not yet known
cases.risk: During a connection's first observation the account id may be null; discarding all evidence then would make early runs permanently unverifiable
cases.setup: CRM evidence with provider_account_id 'hub-001' and an EvaluationContext whose connectedCrmAccountId is null
cases.expected: The assertion is evaluated against the record and returns SUPPORTED rather than RECORD_WRONG_ACCOUNT

cases.requirement: A mandatory assertion supported only by customer_claim evidence is UNKNOWN, never SUPPORTED
cases.risk: This is the product's founding principle in code: the customer's own automation must never grade its own homework
cases.setup: Mandatory `equals` on record.property where the only CRM evidence has origin 'customer_claim'
cases.expected: Result is UNKNOWN with reason_code EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE, and observed_display still shows the claimed value

cases.requirement: An optional assertion may be SUPPORTED by customer_claim evidence, because it cannot change the run outcome
cases.risk: Discarding claim evidence everywhere would strip useful context from reports without improving safety
cases.setup: Optional `equals` on record.property where the only CRM evidence has origin 'customer_claim' and the value matches
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED and the run outcome is unaffected by it

cases.requirement: provider_webhook evidence counts as independent and may support a mandatory assertion
cases.risk: Webhook evidence is signature-verified against the raw bytes; excluding it would make most email assertions unprovable before the deadline
cases.setup: Mandatory `provider_status_in` allowing ['delivered'] where the delivered event has origin 'provider_webhook'
cases.expected: Result is SUPPORTED with reason_code MATCHED

cases.requirement: assertEvaluableRules throws AppError 422 for a rule set with no mandatory assertion
cases.risk: A workflow where nothing is required would return VERIFIED for every run and the customer would be paying for a green light that means nothing
cases.setup: WorkflowRules with two assertions, both mandatory:false
cases.expected: assertEvaluableRules throws AppError with httpStatus 422 and code WORKFLOW_RULES_INVALID

cases.requirement: assertEvaluableRules throws 422 for duplicate rule_id values
cases.risk: Duplicate rule ids collide on the assertions table's UNIQUE(run_id, revision, rule_id) constraint and would silently drop one result
cases.setup: WorkflowRules with two assertions both using rule_id 'crm_exists'
cases.expected: assertEvaluableRules throws AppError 422 WORKFLOW_RULES_INVALID naming the duplicate identifier

cases.requirement: Boundary: exactly LIMITS.MAX_ASSERTIONS_PER_WORKFLOW assertions is accepted and one more is refused
cases.risk: The cap bounds worst-case provider calls per run; letting it drift breaks the published cost ceiling
cases.setup: Two rule sets, one with 10 assertions and one with 11, both otherwise valid
cases.expected: The 10-assertion set evaluates; the 11-assertion set throws AppError 422 WORKFLOW_RULES_INVALID

cases.requirement: workflowRulesSchema rejects a deadline below LIMITS.MIN_DEADLINE_SECONDS and accepts exactly the minimum
cases.risk: A sub-minute deadline would resolve runs before the one-minute cron could ever observe them, producing false failures by design
cases.setup: Rules parsed with deadline_seconds 59 and then 60
cases.expected: 59 fails Zod validation; 60 parses and yields deadline_seconds 60

cases.requirement: workflowRulesSchema rejects a deadline above LIMITS.MAX_DEADLINE_SECONDS and accepts exactly the maximum
cases.risk: An unbounded deadline would hold runs open indefinitely and defeat retention and quota accounting
cases.setup: Rules parsed with deadline_seconds 3601 and then 3600
cases.expected: 3601 fails Zod validation; 3600 parses and yields deadline_seconds 3600

cases.requirement: workflowRulesSchema requires property_name when field is record.property and forbids it otherwise
cases.risk: Without the pairing rule an assertion could address an unnamed property and quietly evaluate undefined forever
cases.setup: Two specs: record.property with no property_name, and record.email with property_name 'company'
cases.expected: Both fail Zod validation with an issue on the property_name path

cases.requirement: workflowRulesSchema rejects a spec whose field belongs to the other evidence source
cases.risk: A crm field read against email evidence would never find a value and would look like a provider outage rather than a configuration error
cases.setup: Spec with source 'email_event' and field 'record.email'
cases.expected: Zod validation fails with an issue on the field path

cases.requirement: A single contradicted mandatory assertion makes the whole run FAILED regardless of how many others passed
cases.risk: A false VERIFIED is the one defect that destroys the product's reason to exist; there is no majority vote over evidence
cases.setup: Three mandatory results: two SUPPORTED, one CONTRADICTED with VALUE_MISMATCH, deadline still open
cases.expected: decideRunStatus returns FAILED with DECISION_REASON.FAILED_CONTRADICTED

cases.requirement: A contradicted optional assertion never changes a run that is otherwise fully supported
cases.risk: If optional checks could fail a run, customers would stop adding informational checks and lose the diagnostic value they exist for
cases.setup: Two mandatory SUPPORTED results plus one optional CONTRADICTED result
cases.expected: decideRunStatus returns VERIFIED with DECISION_REASON.VERIFIED

cases.requirement: decideRunStatus throws AppError 422 when the result set contains no mandatory assertion
cases.risk: Answering VERIFIED to 'did anything have to be true?' is the worst bug this product could ship, so it must fail loudly rather than default
cases.setup: A result array containing only optional assertions, all SUPPORTED
cases.expected: decideRunStatus throws AppError 422 with code WORKFLOW_RULES_INVALID

cases.requirement: Inside the completion window with observation budget left and healthy access, the run stays PENDING
cases.risk: Resolving early would convert an in-flight automation into a reported failure and generate false alerts on every slow workflow
cases.setup: One mandatory UNKNOWN/AWAITING_EVIDENCE result, now before deadlineAt, observationsRemaining 2, hasWorkingEvidenceAccess true
cases.expected: decideRunStatus returns PENDING with DECISION_REASON.PENDING_WINDOW

cases.requirement: Inside the window with broken evidence access, the run stays PENDING but with the access-specific reason
cases.risk: The customer must be able to tell 'we are still looking' from 'we cannot reach your CRM yet' while the window is open
cases.setup: Same inputs as the pending case but hasWorkingEvidenceAccess false
cases.expected: decideRunStatus returns PENDING with DECISION_REASON.PENDING_ACCESS

cases.requirement: After the deadline with broken evidence access, the run is UNVERIFIED and never FAILED
cases.risk: Charging a customer's automation with a failure we could not observe is a false accusation and the exact behaviour competitors get wrong
cases.setup: One mandatory UNKNOWN/CONNECTION_UNAVAILABLE result, now after deadlineAt, hasWorkingEvidenceAccess false
cases.expected: decideRunStatus returns UNVERIFIED with DECISION_REASON.UNVERIFIED_ACCESS

cases.requirement: Boundary: with the observation budget exhausted but the window still open, the run resolves UNVERIFIED rather than FAILED
cases.risk: The record could still be created before the deadline, so absence is not yet a failure even though we have stopped looking
cases.setup: One mandatory UNKNOWN/RECORD_NOT_FOUND result, now before deadlineAt, observationsRemaining 0, healthy access
cases.expected: decideRunStatus returns UNVERIFIED with DECISION_REASON.UNVERIFIED_BUDGET

cases.requirement: After the deadline with healthy access and every unresolved reason an authoritative absence, the run is FAILED
cases.risk: This is the only legitimate route from 'we do not know' to 'it did not happen', and the customer's whole alerting depends on it firing
cases.setup: Mandatory results UNKNOWN/RECORD_NOT_FOUND and UNKNOWN/EVENT_NOT_OBSERVED, now after deadlineAt, healthy access
cases.expected: decideRunStatus returns FAILED with DECISION_REASON.FAILED_ABSENT

cases.requirement: After the deadline with healthy access and a mix of authoritative and non-authoritative absence, the run is UNVERIFIED
cases.risk: One unprovable check must be enough to withhold a failure verdict; a partial proof is not a proof
cases.setup: Mandatory results UNKNOWN/RECORD_NOT_FOUND and UNKNOWN/EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE, now after deadlineAt, healthy access
cases.expected: decideRunStatus returns UNVERIFIED with DECISION_REASON.UNVERIFIED_INCOMPLETE

cases.requirement: Boundary: the deadline comparison is strict, so a decision taken at exactly deadlineAt is treated as outside the window
cases.risk: An ambiguous boundary would make the same evidence resolve differently on two runs of the same code and destroy reproducibility
cases.setup: One mandatory UNKNOWN/RECORD_NOT_FOUND result with ctx.now exactly equal to ctx.deadlineAt and healthy access
cases.expected: decideRunStatus returns FAILED with DECISION_REASON.FAILED_ABSENT rather than PENDING

cases.requirement: summariseMandatory counts only mandatory assertions and never folds optional results into the totals
cases.risk: The report header is built from this summary; including optional checks would show a customer '3 of 4 checks passed' for a VERIFIED run
cases.setup: Two mandatory SUPPORTED results and two optional results, one CONTRADICTED and one UNKNOWN
cases.expected: summariseMandatory reports a total of 2 with 2 supported and 0 contradicted

cases.requirement: nextRunState keeps a PENDING run PENDING on OBSERVATION_RECORDED
cases.risk: An observation that proves nothing must not move the run; otherwise every scheduler tick would churn the status
cases.setup: nextRunState('PENDING', 'OBSERVATION_RECORDED')
cases.expected: Returns 'PENDING' without throwing

cases.requirement: nextRunState moves PENDING to FAILED on MANDATORY_CONTRADICTED
cases.risk: The state machine is the only thing that writes a terminal status; a missing edge would strand contradicted runs in PENDING forever
cases.setup: nextRunState('PENDING', 'MANDATORY_CONTRADICTED')
cases.expected: Returns 'FAILED'

cases.requirement: nextRunState rejects LATE_EVIDENCE_OBSERVED on a PENDING run with a 409
cases.risk: A pending run has no decision to supersede; accepting the event would create a revision that supersedes nothing and corrupt the audit chain
cases.setup: nextRunState('PENDING', 'LATE_EVIDENCE_OBSERVED')
cases.expected: Throws AppError with httpStatus 409 and code ILLEGAL_RUN_TRANSITION

cases.requirement: nextRunState refuses to rewrite a decided run for any event other than late evidence
cases.risk: A decided run is an audit record the customer may have already shown their client; silently rewriting it would make every past report untrustworthy
cases.setup: nextRunState('VERIFIED', 'MANDATORY_CONTRADICTED')
cases.expected: Throws AppError 409 ILLEGAL_RUN_TRANSITION explaining that a decided run is never rewritten

cases.requirement: nextRunState returns a terminal status unchanged for LATE_EVIDENCE_OBSERVED
cases.risk: The existing revision must survive untouched while a new revision records the superseding decision
cases.setup: nextRunState('FAILED', 'LATE_EVIDENCE_OBSERVED')
cases.expected: Returns 'FAILED' without throwing and without mutating the input

cases.requirement: isTerminalRunStatus treats PENDING as non-terminal and the other three statuses as terminal
cases.risk: The scheduler and the retention job both branch on this predicate; a wrong answer either abandons live runs or re-checks decided ones forever
cases.setup: isTerminalRunStatus called for each member of RUN_STATUS
cases.expected: Returns false for PENDING and true for VERIFIED, FAILED and UNVERIFIED

cases.requirement: detectLateCompletion recognises evidence observed after the run's deadline
cases.risk: Late evidence is how an UNVERIFIED run becomes honestly VERIFIED; missing it leaves customers with a permanent unknown that was later resolved
cases.setup: Assertion results whose observed_at values fall after deadlineAt
cases.expected: detectLateCompletion returns true

cases.requirement: detectLateCompletion returns false when every observation predates the deadline
cases.risk: A false positive would spawn pointless revisions on every settled run and inflate the report history
cases.setup: Assertion results whose observed_at values all fall before deadlineAt
cases.expected: detectLateCompletion returns false

cases.requirement: applyLateEvidence records a new revision instead of mutating the existing one
cases.risk: The assertions table is keyed by (run_id, revision, rule_id); mutating in place would destroy the original decision and its evidence links
cases.setup: A run at revision 1 with status UNVERIFIED and a later bundle proving every mandatory assertion
cases.expected: applyLateEvidence returns a revision 2 with status VERIFIED and leaves the revision 1 record unchanged

cases.requirement: applyLateEvidence records no superseding revision when the late evidence reaches the same decision
cases.risk: Revision churn on unchanged outcomes would flood the customer's report history and make real supersessions invisible
cases.setup: A run at revision 1 with status FAILED and late evidence that still yields FAILED
cases.expected: applyLateEvidence reports no change and creates no revision 2

cases.requirement: backoffSeconds grows with the observation count and is capped at MAX_BACKOFF_SECONDS
cases.risk: An uncapped backoff would push the next check past the deadline and silently abandon the run
cases.setup: backoffSeconds evaluated for observation counts 0 through 8 at a fixed jitter
cases.expected: Values increase monotonically and never exceed MAX_BACKOFF_SECONDS (600)

cases.requirement: The schedule is reproducible: the same counters always produce the same delay
cases.risk: A non-deterministic schedule makes every concurrency and deadline test flaky and makes production incidents impossible to reconstruct
cases.setup: planNextObservation called twice with identical inputs in separate evaluations
cases.expected: Both calls return the same nextCheckAt to the millisecond

cases.requirement: planNextObservation schedules nothing for a run that already has a final result
cases.risk: Re-checking a decided run spends provider quota and can only produce a contradiction with an audit record we have promised not to rewrite
cases.setup: planNextObservation for a run whose status is VERIFIED
cases.expected: nextCheckAt is null with SCHEDULE_REASON.DECIDED

cases.requirement: planNextObservation refuses a check that would land after the deadline
cases.risk: Scheduling past the deadline would hold a run open beyond its agreed window and delay the customer's answer indefinitely
cases.setup: A run 30 seconds from its deadline where the computed backoff exceeds the remaining time
cases.expected: nextCheckAt is null with SCHEDULE_REASON.WOULD_EXCEED_DEADLINE

cases.requirement: Boundary: planNextObservation stops at LIMITS.MAX_OBSERVATIONS_PER_RUN
cases.risk: The observation cap is what bounds the published 4,000-call worst case; exceeding it breaks the cost model and the provider rate-limit argument
cases.setup: A run with observationCount already equal to 4 and its window still open
cases.expected: nextCheckAt is null with SCHEDULE_REASON.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED

cases.requirement: planNextObservation honours a provider-supplied retry delay over its own backoff
cases.risk: Ignoring an explicit Retry-After is how an account gets rate-limit banned, which would take out every workspace sharing the connector
cases.setup: A rate-limited gap carrying a retry-after of 120 seconds where the computed backoff would be 30
cases.expected: nextCheckAt is 120 seconds ahead with SCHEDULE_REASON.RETRY_AFTER

cases.requirement: planNextObservation stops scheduling for a terminal connector gap
cases.risk: Retrying an expired authorisation burns quota for an outcome that cannot change until the customer re-authorises
cases.setup: A gap with code AUTH_EXPIRED and retryable false, with observations and window still available
cases.expected: nextCheckAt is null with SCHEDULE_REASON.TERMINAL_GAP

cases.requirement: Boundary: planNextRetry stops at LIMITS.MAX_TRANSIENT_RETRIES_PER_OBSERVATION
cases.risk: Unbounded transport retries multiply provider calls per observation and break the concurrency caps the rate-limit analysis depends on
cases.setup: A retryable PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE failure with attemptsUsed already equal to 3
cases.expected: planNextRetry returns no retry with RETRY_REASON.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED

cases.requirement: planNextRetry refuses to retry a terminal connector error
cases.risk: Retrying PERMISSION_MISSING can never succeed and delays telling the customer the one thing they must fix
cases.setup: A PERMISSION_MISSING failure with retries still available
cases.expected: planNextRetry returns no retry with RETRY_REASON.TERMINAL

cases.requirement: maxExternalCallsPerRun equals the LIMITS arithmetic published in the scope document
cases.risk: The published cost ceiling and the provider rate-limit argument are both built on this number; drift makes a public document untrue
cases.setup: maxExternalCallsPerRun() compared against MAX_OBSERVATIONS_PER_RUN and MAX_TRANSIENT_RETRIES_PER_OBSERVATION
cases.expected: The returned value matches the constant-derived product and does not hard-code a literal

cases.requirement: explainRunStatus returns distinct customer-facing text for all four run statuses
cases.risk: UNVERIFIED reading like FAILED is the misunderstanding that generates support load and cancellations
cases.setup: explainRunStatus called for PENDING, VERIFIED, FAILED and UNVERIFIED
cases.expected: Four distinct explanations, with the UNVERIFIED text stating explicitly that it is not a failure

cases.requirement: explainReasonCode covers every member of REASON_CODE with no generic fallback text
cases.risk: An unexplained reason code renders as a black box, which contradicts the published claim that we show our reasoning in plain language
cases.setup: explainReasonCode called for each of the 14 REASON_CODE members
cases.expected: Every call returns a distinct non-empty explanation and none is a shared default string

cases.requirement: explainRun never includes a raw provider payload or an unmasked email address
cases.risk: The explanation is rendered into the customer report and the export; leaking a raw payload there would breach the redaction rule at the most visible point
cases.setup: explainRun for a run whose evidence carried a full recipient address and CRM property values
cases.expected: The explanation text contains no unmasked address and no verbatim provider payload fragment

cases.requirement: In customer_triggered coverage mode a workflow that receives no event produces no run and no claim of success
cases.risk: Showing '100% success' for a workflow that has received nothing is the exact dishonesty the README promises to avoid
cases.setup: An active workflow in customer_triggered mode with zero source_events over a reporting period
cases.expected: The period summary reports zero runs and renders the no-data state, never a success rate

cases.requirement: In independently_sourced coverage mode an expected trigger that never arrived is surfaced as a missing-run finding
cases.risk: This is the only mode in which the product may claim to detect a run that never started, and it is a paid-for capability
cases.setup: A workflow in independently_sourced mode whose independent source lists an enquiry with no matching source_event
cases.expected: A missing-run finding is raised for that enquiry and it is not reported as a FAILED run

cases.requirement: A workflow's inactivity warning is distinct from any run status and never contributes to the success rate
cases.risk: Merging inactivity into run statistics would let silence look like either success or failure, both of which are untrue
cases.setup: A workflow whose last_event_at is older than its expected_activity setting and which has no runs in the period
cases.expected: An inactivity warning is produced and the period's run statistics remain empty

cases.requirement: The coverage mode is attached to every run record so a report can never be read without it
cases.risk: The scope document requires the coverage caveat to stand beside every result rather than live in a footnote
cases.setup: Runs created under both coverage modes and read back through the reporting query
cases.expected: Each returned run carries its workflow version's coverage_mode value

cases.requirement: A run that resolves UNVERIFIED renders the unverified explanation and is visually distinct from a failure
cases.risk: If the interface makes unverified look like failure, customers will chase their own automations for our access problems
cases.setup: Seeded workspace with one UNVERIFIED run caused by an expired HubSpot connection, viewed on the run report page
cases.expected: The page shows the unverified wording, names the connection problem, and does not use the failure styling or the word failed

cases.requirement: A VERIFIED report lists each mandatory rule with its own evidence reference and observation time
cases.risk: The evidence artefact is what the agency shows their own client in a dispute; a pass with no evidence links is worth nothing
cases.setup: Seeded workspace with one VERIFIED run over three mandatory assertions, viewed on the run report page
cases.expected: Each rule row shows its label, expected display, observed display, observed time and an evidence reference

cases.requirement: The HubSpot adapter translates a contact payload into CrmRecordEvidence with origin provider_readback
cases.risk: Origin is what licenses a mandatory assertion to pass; mislabelling a readback would either block every verification or admit weaker evidence
cases.setup: A stubbed HubSpot contact search response for correlation value 'enq-1001'
cases.expected: A CrmRecordEvidence is returned with origin 'provider_readback', the record id, email and correlation value populated

cases.requirement: The adapter reads the correlation value from the workspace's configured crm_correlation_property, not a hard-coded name
cases.risk: Every customer names their property differently; a hard-coded name would silently verify against a property that does not exist
cases.setup: Workflow rules with crm_correlation_property 'verify_enquiry_ref' and a contact payload carrying that property
cases.expected: The returned evidence's correlation_value is taken from verify_enquiry_ref

cases.requirement: The adapter carries the provider account id through to the evidence so the account gate can run
cases.risk: Without the account id the evaluator cannot tell a foreign record from the customer's own, and cross-account evidence would be accepted
cases.setup: A HubSpot response accompanied by the connection's external_account_id
cases.expected: CrmRecordEvidence.provider_account_id equals the connection's external_account_id

cases.requirement: A search returning two contacts for one correlation value yields an AMBIGUOUS_MATCH gap and no record
cases.risk: Picking one of two candidate records is a coin flip that can produce a false VERIFIED against the wrong customer's data
cases.setup: A stubbed HubSpot search response containing two contacts with the same correlation value
cases.expected: The bundle carries a gap {source:'crm_record', code:'AMBIGUOUS_MATCH', retryable:false} and crm is null

cases.requirement: A search returning zero contacts yields a NOT_FOUND gap that is explicitly non-retryable
cases.risk: NOT_FOUND is the only path to an authoritative absence; marking it retryable would waste the observation budget and prevent a legitimate FAILED
cases.setup: A stubbed HubSpot search response with an empty results array
cases.expected: The bundle carries a gap {source:'crm_record', code:'NOT_FOUND', retryable:false}

cases.requirement: A 401 from HubSpot maps to AUTH_EXPIRED, a terminal connector error
cases.risk: Retrying an expired token burns quota and hides the one action the customer must take
cases.setup: A stubbed HubSpot response with HTTP 401
cases.expected: The adapter returns the connector error code AUTH_EXPIRED and isRetryableConnectorError reports false

cases.requirement: A 403 from HubSpot maps to PERMISSION_MISSING rather than NOT_FOUND
cases.risk: A missing scope looks like an empty CRM; conflating them would report the customer's automation as broken when our access is the problem
cases.setup: A stubbed HubSpot response with HTTP 403 and a scope error body
cases.expected: The adapter returns PERMISSION_MISSING and the connection is marked degraded rather than the record marked absent

cases.requirement: A 429 from HubSpot maps to RATE_LIMITED and the Retry-After header is surfaced to the scheduler
cases.risk: Ignoring an explicit back-off is how the shared app registration gets throttled for every customer at once
cases.setup: A stubbed HubSpot response with HTTP 429 and Retry-After 30
cases.expected: The adapter returns RATE_LIMITED with a retry-after of 30 seconds and isRetryableConnectorError reports true

cases.requirement: A 500 from HubSpot maps to PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE and is retryable
cases.risk: A provider blip must not become a customer-visible failure verdict about their automation
cases.setup: A stubbed HubSpot response with HTTP 500 and an HTML error body
cases.expected: The adapter returns PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, retryable true, and no evidence is fabricated

cases.requirement: A HubSpot payload missing the properties object entirely yields INVALID_EVIDENCE, not a partially-built record
cases.risk: A half-built evidence record would be evaluated as an authoritative empty and could contradict a rule that was never actually checked
cases.setup: A stubbed HubSpot 200 response whose body has an id but no properties key
cases.expected: The adapter returns INVALID_EVIDENCE and produces no CrmRecordEvidence

cases.requirement: A HubSpot payload with a non-string property value is coerced to null rather than accepted as a value
cases.risk: A numeric or object value compared with a string expectation would produce an arbitrary verdict from a type confusion
cases.setup: A stubbed contact whose 'lead_score' property is the number 42
cases.expected: The evidence records lead_score as null and the adapter logs an invalid-evidence note rather than stringifying it silently

cases.requirement: The adapter never requests a write scope and issues no non-GET call to HubSpot
cases.risk: The product's central promise is that it never modifies the customer's CRM; a single write call would falsify it publicly
cases.setup: Every HubSpot adapter entry point exercised against a recording fetch stub
cases.expected: The recorded requests contain only read methods and the requested scope list contains no write scope

cases.requirement: The adapter only ever calls hosts on the fixed provider allowlist
cases.risk: Engineering rule 8 forbids fetching a customer-controlled URL; a connector that follows a payload-supplied host is an SSRF path into our Worker
cases.setup: A HubSpot response body containing a next-page link pointing at an attacker-controlled host
cases.expected: The adapter refuses the off-allowlist host and returns INVALID_EVIDENCE rather than following the link

cases.requirement: The adapter bounds its response reading so an oversized provider body cannot exhaust Worker memory
cases.risk: An unbounded read from a third party is a denial-of-service vector we do not control
cases.setup: A stubbed HubSpot response whose body exceeds the adapter's read cap
cases.expected: The adapter aborts the read and returns INVALID_EVIDENCE without buffering the whole body

cases.requirement: The Resend adapter maps each provider event to an EmailEventEvidence with a normalised EMAIL_STATUS value
cases.risk: The evaluator only understands the normalised vocabulary; an unmapped provider word would silently never match any rule
cases.setup: A stubbed Resend events response containing email.sent and email.delivered entries
cases.expected: Two EmailEventEvidence records are returned with statuses drawn from EMAIL_STATUS in observation order

cases.requirement: Resend's 'email.sent' maps to 'accepted', never to 'delivered'
cases.risk: This single mapping is where a false delivery claim would enter the system, and the product publicly distinguishes the two
cases.setup: A stubbed Resend events response whose only entry is email.sent
cases.expected: The evidence status is 'accepted' and DELIVERY_PROVING_STATUSES does not contain it

cases.requirement: Resend's bounce event maps to 'bounced' and is preserved even when a later event arrives
cases.risk: Dropping a bounce because a subsequent engagement event exists would erase the definitive failure the customer needs
cases.setup: A stubbed events response containing email.delivered followed by email.bounced
cases.expected: Both events appear in the returned ladder with their original order and timestamps

cases.requirement: An unrecognised Resend event type is dropped with an INVALID_EVIDENCE note rather than guessed
cases.risk: Guessing a status from an unknown provider word is exactly how a new provider feature becomes a false VERIFIED
cases.setup: A stubbed events response containing an entry of type 'email.something_new'
cases.expected: The unknown entry produces no evidence and an INVALID_EVIDENCE gap is recorded for the source

cases.requirement: A Resend event with an unparseable occurred_at is rejected rather than defaulted to now
cases.risk: Defaulting a timestamp to now would make every occurred_within rule pass regardless of when the email actually happened
cases.setup: A stubbed events response whose entry has created_at 'yesterday'
cases.expected: The entry is dropped with an INVALID_EVIDENCE note and no evidence is produced with a substituted timestamp

cases.requirement: A 401 from Resend maps to AUTH_EXPIRED and the email half of the bundle reports a gap, not an absence
cases.risk: Reporting our own revoked API key as 'no email was sent' would be a false accusation against the customer's automation
cases.setup: A stubbed Resend response with HTTP 401
cases.expected: The bundle carries a gap {source:'email_event', code:'AUTH_EXPIRED'} and email_events is empty

cases.requirement: A 429 from Resend maps to RATE_LIMITED with its retry delay preserved
cases.risk: Resend documents 10 requests per second per team; ignoring the back-off risks the customer's own sending account
cases.setup: A stubbed Resend response with HTTP 429 and a rate-limit reset header
cases.expected: The adapter returns RATE_LIMITED and surfaces the reset delay to the scheduler

cases.requirement: A Resend response for a message id that belongs to another account yields RECORD_WRONG_ACCOUNT-capable evidence
cases.risk: Cross-account email evidence would let one customer's delivery prove another customer's workflow
cases.setup: A stubbed events response whose entries carry a provider account id other than the connection's
cases.expected: The evidence records the foreign account id so the evaluator's account gate can contradict it

cases.requirement: The adapter never calls a Resend send endpoint
cases.risk: The product promises it never sends replacement emails; a send call would both break that promise and spend the customer's sending quota
cases.setup: Every Resend adapter entry point exercised against a recording fetch stub
cases.expected: No recorded request targets a send path and no request body contains a message payload

cases.requirement: Every adapter returns a ConnectorErrorCode drawn from the frozen CONNECTOR_ERROR_CODE tuple
cases.risk: An unrecognised error code falls through the scheduler's branching and produces unpredictable retry behaviour
cases.setup: Each adapter driven through its full stubbed failure matrix
cases.expected: Every returned error code is a member of CONNECTOR_ERROR_CODE

cases.requirement: isRetryableConnectorError agrees with each adapter's own retryable flag for every code it emits
cases.risk: A disagreement between the contract and the adapter means the scheduler and the reporter tell the customer different stories about the same failure
cases.setup: Each emitted gap compared against isRetryableConnectorError for its code
cases.expected: The gap's retryable flag matches the contract helper for all eight codes

cases.requirement: A connector error message never contains the credential, the bearer token or any provider secret
cases.risk: Connector errors reach logs, the run report and the export; a leaked token there is a full account compromise
cases.setup: Each adapter failing with a stubbed response whose body echoes the Authorization header
cases.expected: No returned error detail, log line or evidence field contains the token value

cases.requirement: A connector request carries a bounded timeout and reports PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE when it elapses
cases.risk: An unbounded provider call would hold a Worker invocation open and stall the whole one-minute scheduler tick
cases.setup: A fetch stub that never settles
cases.expected: The adapter aborts at its configured timeout and returns PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE

cases.requirement: A UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY error is returned when a rule addresses a field the provider plan cannot expose
cases.risk: Telling a customer 'unknown' forever for a property their plan does not return is a support burden with no route to resolution
cases.setup: A workflow rule addressing a CRM property the stubbed account tier does not expose
cases.expected: The adapter returns UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY and the connection is shown as unsupported rather than degraded

cases.requirement: An observation collects CRM and email evidence into a single EvidenceBundle with per-source gaps
cases.risk: The evaluator reads one bundle; a bundle assembled wrongly makes every downstream verdict wrong regardless of correct adapters
cases.setup: Both adapters stubbed, CRM returning a record and Resend returning a 429
cases.expected: The bundle has crm populated, email_events empty and exactly one gap on source email_event

cases.requirement: An observation that fails on one source still records the evidence retrieved from the other
cases.risk: Discarding good CRM evidence because the email provider was down wastes the call and delays a verdict the customer could have had
cases.setup: CRM adapter succeeding, Resend adapter returning PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE
cases.expected: The stored evidence row for the CRM record exists and the run remains PENDING with an email-source gap

cases.requirement: Observation respects LIMITS.MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTOR_REQUESTS_PER_WORKSPACE
cases.risk: The published provider rate-limit argument depends on this cap; exceeding it is what triggers a throttle that affects every workspace
cases.setup: Six runs for one workspace due in the same scheduler tick with a counting fetch stub
cases.expected: At most 2 connector requests for that workspace are in flight at any instant

cases.requirement: Observation respects LIMITS.MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTOR_REQUESTS_GLOBAL across workspaces
cases.risk: A global burst from many small workspaces would hit the shared HubSpot app registration limit that no single workspace cap can prevent
cases.setup: Twelve runs across six workspaces due in the same tick with a counting fetch stub
cases.expected: At most 5 connector requests are in flight globally at any instant

cases.requirement: Evidence is persisted as a redacted summary and a content digest, never as the raw provider payload
cases.risk: The evidence table is exported and shown in reports; storing raw payloads would put customer PII beyond our redaction boundary
cases.setup: An observation whose HubSpot payload contains a full email address and a free-text note
cases.expected: The stored evidence row's redacted_summary contains masked values only and no field holds the verbatim payload

cases.requirement: Stored evidence carries an expires_at exactly LIMITS.EVIDENCE_RETENTION_DAYS ahead of observation
cases.risk: The 30-day retention claim is public; evidence that outlives it is a data-protection commitment broken in writing
cases.setup: An observation performed at a fixed clock
cases.expected: The evidence row's expires_at equals observed_at plus 30 days

cases.requirement: A late-arriving email event produces a new evidence row rather than mutating the earlier one
cases.risk: The evidence chain has to show what we knew and when; overwriting it makes the audit trail a fiction
cases.setup: An accepted event stored at observation 1, then a delivered event for the same message at observation 2
cases.expected: Two evidence rows exist with distinct content digests and both are linked to the run

cases.requirement: An identical provider payload observed twice produces one evidence row, matched on content digest
cases.risk: Duplicate evidence rows inflate the retention footprint and make the report show the same fact several times
cases.setup: Two observations returning byte-identical Resend payloads
cases.expected: Exactly one evidence row exists for that digest and the second observation records no new row

cases.requirement: A HubSpot webhook with a valid signature over the raw bytes produces provider_webhook evidence
cases.risk: Signature verification against the raw body is the only thing that distinguishes provider evidence from an attacker's post
cases.setup: A signed HubSpot webhook request with a correct v3 signature
cases.expected: A webhook_receipts row with processing_status 'processed' and evidence created with origin provider_webhook

cases.requirement: A webhook whose signature is computed over a re-serialised body is rejected
cases.risk: Verifying a parsed-and-re-serialised body accepts any semantically equal payload, which defeats the signature entirely
cases.setup: A webhook whose JSON is byte-different but semantically identical to the signed payload
cases.expected: The request is rejected, the receipt is recorded as 'invalid' and no evidence is created

cases.requirement: A webhook replayed outside the signature tolerance window is rejected
cases.risk: A captured webhook replayed days later could resurrect stale evidence for a decided run
cases.setup: A correctly signed webhook whose timestamp is older than the tolerance
cases.expected: The request is rejected as invalid and the receipt records the reason without creating evidence

cases.requirement: A duplicate webhook for the same (provider, event_id) is recorded once and processed once
cases.risk: Providers retry webhooks; a second effect from a retry would double-count evidence and could flip a decided run
cases.setup: The same signed webhook delivered three times
cases.expected: Exactly one webhook_receipts row exists, later deliveries are recorded as duplicate, and evidence is created once

cases.requirement: A webhook for an unknown connection is ignored rather than attributed to any workspace
cases.risk: Guessing the workspace for an unattributable webhook is a cross-tenant data write
cases.setup: A correctly signed webhook whose account id matches no connection row
cases.expected: The receipt is recorded with processing_status 'ignored', workspace_id null, and no evidence row is written

cases.requirement: A connection moves through authorising to testing to ready only after a successful capability probe
cases.risk: Marking a connection ready before proving read access produces runs that fail on their first observation
cases.setup: A new HubSpot connection completing authorisation with a stubbed successful probe
cases.expected: The connection status ends as 'ready' and last_check_at is set; no run is accepted before that

cases.requirement: A connection whose probe returns PERMISSION_MISSING ends in 'degraded' with the error code recorded
cases.risk: A silently half-working connection produces permanent unknowns the customer cannot diagnose
cases.setup: A new connection whose stubbed probe returns HTTP 403
cases.expected: Connection status is 'degraded' with last_error_code PERMISSION_MISSING and the UI blocks activation

cases.requirement: Revoking a connection retires its credential versions and stops further observations immediately
cases.risk: A revoked connection that keeps polling is an unauthorised use of the customer's provider account
cases.setup: A ready connection revoked while two runs are PENDING against it
cases.expected: Connection status is 'revoked', its credential_versions rows carry retired_at, and the next tick performs no provider call for those runs

cases.requirement: Revoking and reconnecting the same provider reuses the UNIQUE(workspace_id, provider) row rather than creating a second
cases.risk: A duplicate connection row would leave two credentials live for one provider and make revocation incomplete
cases.setup: A revoked HubSpot connection followed by a fresh authorisation in the same workspace
cases.expected: One connections row exists for (workspace, 'hubspot') with status ready and a new credential version

cases.requirement: A connection that repeatedly returns retryable errors is marked degraded without losing its credentials
cases.risk: Dropping credentials on a transient provider outage would force every affected customer to re-authorise for no reason
cases.setup: Five consecutive observations returning PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE for one connection
cases.expected: The connection is marked degraded, its credential versions remain active, and it recovers to ready on the next success

cases.requirement: A workspace cannot read or use a connection belonging to another workspace
cases.risk: Cross-tenant connector use would read one customer's CRM with another's credentials — the worst possible breach for this product
cases.setup: A run in workspace B referencing a connection id owned by workspace A
cases.expected: The lookup returns nothing, the run records CONNECTION_UNAVAILABLE, and no provider call is made with workspace A's credentials

cases.requirement: The connections page shows each provider's status in plain language with the action the customer must take
cases.risk: A status word with no next action is the single biggest driver of setup abandonment for a product that needs two connections before it does anything
cases.setup: Seeded workspace with HubSpot 'ready' and Resend 'expired', viewed on the connections page
cases.expected: Each connection shows its state in plain words and the expired one offers a reconnect action

cases.requirement: A customer cannot activate a workflow while either connection is not ready
cases.risk: Accepting events with no working evidence access produces a stream of unverified runs and an immediate refund request
cases.setup: Seeded workspace with a valid workflow draft and Resend still in 'authorising', attempting to activate
cases.expected: Activation is refused with an explanation naming the connection that is not ready

cases.requirement: A real HubSpot sandbox read returns a contact whose shape matches CrmRecordEvidence
cases.risk: Every other connector test uses a stub; without one authorised real call we have no evidence the payload shape assumption holds at all
cases.setup: A single authorised read against a HubSpot developer test account seeded with one contact, run only when the provider credential is present
cases.expected: The adapter produces valid CrmRecordEvidence from the real response and the test is skipped, not failed, when the credential is absent

cases.requirement: A real Resend test-mode event read returns a status the adapter can map into EMAIL_STATUS
cases.risk: Resend's event vocabulary is the one mapping most likely to drift; a mock can never detect a renamed event type
cases.setup: A single authorised read against a Resend test account for one previously sent test message, run only when the provider credential is present
cases.expected: Every returned event type maps to a member of EMAIL_STATUS, and the test is skipped when the credential is absent

cases.requirement: A repeated source event with the same external_event_id returns the original run rather than creating a second
cases.risk: A retrying customer automation would otherwise consume two runs of a 500-run allowance and produce two contradictory reports for one enquiry
cases.setup: The same signed source event POSTed twice to /api/v1/events for one workspace
cases.expected: Both responses carry the same run_id, the second has duplicate true, and exactly one runs row exists

cases.requirement: The idempotency key is scoped per workspace, so two workspaces may legitimately use the same external_event_id
cases.risk: A global key space would let one customer's event id block another customer's enquiry entirely
cases.setup: Two workspaces each POSTing an event with external_event_id 'enq-1001'
cases.expected: Two distinct source_events and two distinct runs exist, one per workspace

cases.requirement: A duplicate event whose payload differs from the original is rejected with 409 rather than silently accepted
cases.risk: Reusing an event id with different expectations would let a customer retroactively change what a decided run was checked against
cases.setup: An event id reused with a different correlation_id in the same workspace
cases.expected: The response is 409, the original run is unchanged, and no second source_events row is written

cases.requirement: The UNIQUE(workspace_id, external_event_id) constraint is the enforcement, not an application pre-check alone
cases.risk: A read-then-write check loses the race under concurrency; the database constraint is the only thing that holds
cases.setup: Two concurrent inserts of the same (workspace_id, external_event_id) pair
cases.expected: One insert succeeds, the other raises the constraint violation, and the handler converts it into the duplicate response

cases.requirement: The runs table's UNIQUE source_event_id prevents two runs from ever being created for one source event
cases.risk: Two runs for one enquiry would double-charge the allowance and present the customer with two answers to one question
cases.setup: Two concurrent attempts to create a run from the same source_events row
cases.expected: Exactly one runs row exists and the losing attempt returns the existing run

cases.requirement: An order's idempotency_key is UNIQUE, so a retried checkout creation returns the original checkout session
cases.risk: A duplicate checkout is a duplicate charge; this is the highest-consequence idempotency path in the product
cases.setup: Two checkout creations issued with the same idempotency key for one workspace
cases.expected: One orders row exists and both calls return the same checkout_session_id

cases.requirement: A refund's idempotency_key is UNIQUE, so a retried refund request never issues a second refund
cases.risk: A double refund is money leaving the business with no way to reclaim it
cases.setup: Two refund requests submitted with the same idempotency key
cases.expected: One refunds row exists and the second request returns the existing refund state

cases.requirement: A budget entry's idempotency_key is UNIQUE, so a retried reservation does not reserve twice
cases.risk: Double reservation silently shrinks the available budget and can block spending the founder has already authorised
cases.setup: Two reserve entries written with the same idempotency key against one budget account
cases.expected: One budget_entries row exists and the account's reserved_minor reflects a single reservation

cases.requirement: An outbox unique_event_key is UNIQUE, so the same domain event is enqueued once
cases.risk: Duplicate outbox rows produce duplicate notifications, which for an email notification means spamming a customer
cases.setup: Two attempts to enqueue the same (event_type, entity_id) domain event
cases.expected: One outbox row exists and the second attempt is a no-op that does not raise to the caller

cases.requirement: A notification_deliveries notification_key is UNIQUE, so a retried send does not email the customer twice
cases.risk: Duplicate operational email is the fastest route to a spam complaint against our own sending domain
cases.setup: Two dispatch attempts for the same notification key after a crash between send and state update
cases.expected: One notification_deliveries row exists and the second attempt observes the existing 'sent' state

cases.requirement: A due run is claimed by exactly one scheduler tick under concurrent dispatch
cases.risk: Two workers observing the same run at once would double the provider calls and could write conflicting assertion revisions
cases.setup: Two concurrent dispatchers over one due run with a conditional lease update
cases.expected: Exactly one dispatcher acquires the lease; the other observes zero rows updated and skips the run

cases.requirement: A lease whose expiry has passed is reclaimable by a later tick
cases.risk: A crash mid-observation would otherwise strand the run forever, and the customer would never get an answer
cases.setup: A run_attempts row with lease_expires_at in the past and no ended_at
cases.expected: The next dispatcher claims the run, writes a new lease id and increments attempt_number

cases.requirement: A lease that is still live is not reclaimed by a concurrent tick
cases.risk: Stealing a live lease reintroduces the double-observation problem the lease exists to prevent
cases.setup: A run_attempts row with lease_expires_at 30 seconds in the future
cases.expected: A second dispatcher does not claim the run and no second attempt row is created

cases.requirement: Reclaiming a lease creates a new attempt row rather than reusing the abandoned one
cases.risk: Reusing the row hides the crash, and the UNIQUE(run_id, attempt_number) constraint is what makes the attempt history readable
cases.setup: A reclaimed run whose previous attempt was attempt_number 1
cases.expected: A new run_attempts row exists with attempt_number 2 and the original row retains its outcome fields

cases.requirement: An observation that crashes after the provider call but before the assertion write leaves the run re-observable
cases.risk: A half-applied observation that blocks retries would strand a paying customer's run at PENDING until its deadline
cases.setup: A dispatcher that throws after fetching evidence and before committing assertions
cases.expected: No assertions rows are written for that revision, the lease expires, and the next tick re-observes the run

cases.requirement: An observation that crashes after committing assertions does not re-apply them on retry
cases.risk: Re-applying would violate UNIQUE(run_id, revision, rule_id) and could abort the whole subsequent tick
cases.setup: A dispatcher that commits assertions and then throws before clearing its lease
cases.expected: The retry observes the existing revision, does not attempt a duplicate insert, and proceeds to the decision step

cases.requirement: The due-job query uses the partial index on next_check_at and never performs a full table scan
cases.risk: A full scan on a growing runs table would blow the Worker CPU budget every minute and eventually stop all verification
cases.setup: A seeded runs table with 20,000 terminal runs and 5 due runs, queried through the dispatcher
cases.expected: The query plan uses idx_runs_due and returns only the 5 due runs

cases.requirement: The dispatcher processes a bounded batch per tick rather than every due run
cases.risk: An unbounded batch after an outage would exceed the Worker's time limit and never complete, permanently wedging the queue
cases.setup: A seeded runs table with 500 simultaneously due runs
cases.expected: The tick claims at most its configured batch size and leaves the remainder due for the next tick

cases.requirement: A terminal run has next_check_at set to NULL so the scheduler never reconsiders it
cases.risk: Re-checking decided runs spends provider quota and risks contradicting an audit record we have promised never to rewrite
cases.setup: A run transitioning to VERIFIED through the scheduler
cases.expected: The runs row has next_check_at NULL and does not appear in the next due-job query

cases.requirement: An outbox row is written in the same transaction as the state change that caused it
cases.risk: A state change with no outbox row means a customer never learns their run failed; an outbox row with no state change notifies about something that did not happen
cases.setup: A run transition to FAILED whose outbox insert is observed with the run update
cases.expected: Either both rows are present or neither is, with no interleaving visible to a concurrent reader

cases.requirement: A dispatched outbox row moves to 'dispatched' and is not dispatched again
cases.risk: Repeat dispatch means repeat customer notification for one event
cases.setup: An outbox row dispatched successfully then re-examined by the next tick
cases.expected: The row's dispatch_state is 'dispatched' and it is excluded by the partial index on pending rows

cases.requirement: A failing outbox dispatch backs off using next_attempt_at rather than retrying every tick
cases.risk: Hot-looping a failing dispatch burns the per-minute Worker budget and can starve verification work
cases.setup: An outbox row whose dispatch throws twice in succession
cases.expected: attempts increments, next_attempt_at moves further ahead each time, and the row is skipped until then

cases.requirement: An outbox row that exceeds its attempt budget moves to 'dead' rather than retrying forever
cases.risk: A permanently poisoned row would consume a dispatch slot on every tick indefinitely
cases.setup: An outbox row failing past its configured maximum attempts
cases.expected: dispatch_state becomes 'dead', last_error is recorded, and the row is excluded from the due query

cases.requirement: Outbox dispatch is idempotent at the effect boundary, so a duplicated dispatch causes one effect
cases.risk: At-least-once delivery is the design; without effect-level idempotency the design produces duplicate customer emails
cases.setup: The same outbox row dispatched twice by an interleaved tick
cases.expected: The downstream effect records exactly one notification_deliveries row for the derived notification key

cases.requirement: A run, its assertions and its evidence links are committed atomically
cases.risk: A run with missing assertions renders an empty report that tells the customer nothing while claiming a verdict
cases.setup: A write path interrupted between the run update and the assertion inserts
cases.expected: A concurrent reader never sees a decided run with an incomplete assertion set for that revision

cases.requirement: A failed transaction leaves no partial row behind in any table it touched
cases.risk: Orphan rows accumulate silently and later produce phantom entries in reports and exports
cases.setup: A multi-table write whose final statement violates a CHECK constraint
cases.expected: No rows from that transaction are present in any of the affected tables

cases.requirement: Every customer-scoped read includes workspace_id in its WHERE clause
cases.risk: Tenant scope is application-enforced; a single query missing the predicate is a cross-tenant data leak with no database backstop
cases.setup: Static inspection of every exported query in apps/app/src/db plus a runtime probe reading each accessor with a foreign workspace id
cases.expected: Every accessor returns nothing for a foreign workspace and no query string omits the workspace_id predicate

cases.requirement: A composite lookup proves the child belongs to the parent within the same workspace
cases.risk: Checking only the child id lets a caller read another workspace's run by guessing an id under their own workflow
cases.setup: Reading a run by (workspace_id, workflow_id, run_id) where the run belongs to a different workflow
cases.expected: The lookup returns nothing rather than the run

cases.requirement: Writing a row with a status value outside its CHECK constraint is rejected by the database
cases.risk: A fifth run status in the data would break every consumer that switches on the four, including the report renderer
cases.setup: An attempt to insert a runs row with status 'SUCCESS'
cases.expected: The insert fails on the CHECK constraint and no row is written

cases.requirement: A workspace delete cascades to its memberships, connections, workflows, runs and evidence
cases.risk: Residual customer data after a deletion request is a data-protection failure we have committed in writing not to make
cases.setup: A populated workspace deleted through the deletion path
cases.expected: No rows referencing that workspace_id remain in any customer-scoped table

cases.requirement: Deleting a workspace does not delete rows belonging to any other workspace
cases.risk: A cascade that over-reaches would destroy a paying customer's data during another customer's deletion
cases.setup: Two populated workspaces where one is deleted
