cases.expected: The second workspace's row counts are unchanged in every table

cases.requirement: Two concurrent event submissions at the allowance boundary consume the allowance exactly once each
cases.risk: A lost update at the boundary either gives away free runs or rejects a run the customer paid for
cases.setup: An entitlements row with run_limit 500 and consumed 498, with four concurrent event submissions
cases.expected: Exactly two submissions are accepted, two are refused, and consumed ends at 500

cases.requirement: Boundary: the 500th run of a period is accepted and the 501st is refused
cases.risk: LIMITS.PLAN_RUNS_PER_PERIOD is a published commercial promise; an off-by-one either short-changes or over-serves every customer
cases.setup: An entitlements row with run_limit 500 and consumed 499, then two sequential submissions
cases.expected: The first is accepted taking consumed to 500; the second is refused with a quota error and consumed stays at 500

cases.requirement: A reservation released after a rejected run returns the allowance rather than consuming it
cases.risk: Charging a customer's allowance for a run we refused to create is taking something for nothing
cases.setup: A submission that reserves allowance and then fails validation before the run is created
cases.expected: The entitlements row's reserved returns to its prior value and consumed is unchanged

cases.requirement: Allowance is tracked per (workspace_id, billing_period) so a new period starts clean
cases.risk: A carried-over counter would lock out a paying customer at the start of their new month
cases.setup: A workspace at its limit in period 2026-09 submitting an event dated in period 2026-10
cases.expected: The submission is accepted against a new entitlements row for 2026-10 with consumed 1

cases.requirement: A workspace with no active entitlement cannot consume allowance from another workspace's row
cases.risk: Cross-tenant quota consumption would let one customer exhaust another's paid allowance
cases.setup: An event submission for workspace B whose only entitlements row belongs to workspace A
cases.expected: The submission is refused and workspace A's consumed value is unchanged

cases.requirement: The retention job deletes evidence rows past expires_at and leaves the run and assertion records intact
cases.risk: Deleting the verdict alongside the evidence would erase the customer's report history they may still need
cases.setup: Evidence rows aged past 30 days alongside their runs
cases.expected: The expired evidence rows are gone, the runs and assertions remain, and the assertion rows show the evidence as expired rather than missing

cases.requirement: The retention job deletes a bounded batch per tick
cases.risk: An unbounded delete after a backlog would exceed the Worker's limits and never complete, leaving data past its stated retention
cases.setup: 60,000 expired evidence rows and a single scheduler tick
cases.expected: At most the configured batch size is deleted and the remainder is deleted on subsequent ticks

cases.requirement: Expired visit_sessions and rate_limits rows are removed on the same schedule
cases.risk: Unbounded growth in these tables slows every request and breaks the aggregate-only analytics commitment
cases.setup: Seeded expired rows in both tables and one retention tick
cases.expected: Both tables lose only their expired rows and current rows are untouched

cases.requirement: Applying 0001_init.sql to an empty database produces every table, index and constraint the application queries
cases.risk: A missing index is a silent performance cliff; a missing constraint is a silent correctness hole
cases.setup: A fresh D1 database with the migration applied, inspected through sqlite_master
cases.expected: Every table and index named in the migration exists and the schema_migrations row for version 1 is present

cases.requirement: Applying the migration set twice is a no-op rather than an error
cases.risk: A deploy that re-runs migrations must not fail the release or partially reapply a change
cases.setup: The migration runner invoked twice against the same database
cases.expected: The second run applies nothing, reports it, and leaves the schema and schema_migrations unchanged

cases.requirement: Every application query runs successfully against the schema produced by the migrations alone
cases.risk: A query written against a developer's hand-edited local database will fail on first contact with production
cases.setup: Each exported db accessor executed against a freshly migrated database with seeded rows
cases.expected: No query raises a no-such-column or no-such-table error

cases.requirement: No money column in the schema is declared REAL
cases.risk: Floating-point money near a cap or a price is the arithmetic error class this product cannot afford
cases.setup: Schema inspection of every column whose name ends in _minor or holds an amount
cases.expected: Every such column has INTEGER affinity

cases.requirement: The monotonic provider_event_created guard prevents an older Stripe event from overwriting newer subscription state
cases.risk: Stripe delivers webhooks out of order; without the guard a stale 'past_due' can overwrite a current 'active' and lock a paying customer out
cases.setup: A subscriptions row updated by event created 200 then by event created 100
cases.expected: The row retains the state from event 200 and the older event is recorded as ignored

cases.requirement: The unique_event_key builder produces a stable key for the same logical event and distinct keys for different ones
cases.risk: The outbox's whole duplicate-suppression rests on this string; an unstable key suppresses nothing and a colliding key drops real events
cases.setup: Key generation for two identical domain events and for two events differing only in entity id
cases.expected: The identical pair produce equal keys and the differing pair produce different keys

cases.requirement: Generated identifiers are unique across a large batch and carry no guessable sequence
cases.risk: A guessable run id combined with any tenancy mistake turns a scoping bug into an enumeration attack
cases.setup: 100,000 generated ids from apps/app/src/lib/ids
cases.expected: No duplicates appear and consecutive ids differ beyond a monotonic counter suffix

cases.requirement: Time helpers serialise to ISO-8601 UTC strings and reject a local-time input
cases.risk: A local-time string in a deadline comparison shifts every verdict by the server's offset and is invisible in review
cases.setup: Round-tripping a Date through the time helpers and passing a string with no offset
cases.expected: The output always ends in Z and the offsetless input is rejected rather than assumed UTC

cases.requirement: The run history page shows the same run once after the customer's automation retried its submission
cases.risk: A customer who sees their one enquiry listed three times concludes the product is counting their allowance wrongly
cases.setup: Seeded workspace where the same external_event_id was submitted three times
cases.expected: The history lists one run and its detail page notes the duplicate submissions

cases.requirement: A run superseded by late evidence shows both revisions with the later one marked current
cases.risk: Hiding the original decision would make the report look edited; hiding the revision would make it look wrong
cases.setup: Seeded workspace with a run at revision 1 UNVERIFIED and revision 2 VERIFIED
cases.expected: Both revisions are visible with their timestamps and the current one is clearly marked

cases.requirement: A session cookie value is stored only as a hash, so the sessions table cannot be used to impersonate anyone
cases.risk: A database read — a backup, a support query, a leaked export — would otherwise hand over live sessions for every customer
cases.setup: A session created through the session helper, with the returned cookie value compared against the stored id
cases.expected: The stored id is a hash of the cookie value and the plaintext value appears in no column

cases.requirement: Session lookup compares hashes in constant time
cases.risk: A timing oracle on session lookup turns an opaque token into a guessable one
cases.setup: hashToken output compared through timingSafeEqual for matching and near-matching values
cases.expected: Comparison uses timingSafeEqual and does not short-circuit on the first differing byte

cases.requirement: hashToken is domain-separated so a session hash and an invitation hash of the same string differ
cases.risk: Without domain separation a token captured in one context could be replayed in another
cases.setup: hashToken('abc','session') compared with hashToken('abc','invite')
cases.expected: The two digests differ

cases.requirement: A session cookie is issued with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite and the __Host- prefix
cases.risk: A cookie readable by script or sent cross-site is an account takeover from any XSS or CSRF weakness elsewhere
cases.setup: The Set-Cookie header produced by the login path
cases.expected: The header carries HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax or stricter, Path=/ and the __Host- name prefix

cases.requirement: generateCsrfToken produces unpredictable tokens of adequate length
cases.risk: A guessable CSRF token makes every state-changing form forgeable from any site the customer visits
cases.setup: 1,000 generated tokens inspected for length and collisions
cases.expected: All tokens are distinct and meet the configured minimum entropy length

cases.requirement: validateCsrfToken rejects a missing, empty or mismatched token
cases.risk: A validator that treats absence as valid is worse than no validator, because it makes the protection look present in review
cases.setup: Validation attempted with no cookie, no field, an empty field and a mismatched pair
cases.expected: Every case is rejected and only the matching pair is accepted

cases.requirement: isStateChangingMethod classifies POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE as state-changing and GET and HEAD as not
cases.risk: Missing a method here silently exempts a whole class of mutations from CSRF protection
cases.setup: isStateChangingMethod called for each HTTP method
cases.expected: The four mutating methods return true and the safe methods return false

cases.requirement: isSameOriginRequest rejects an Origin header whose host merely prefixes the expected origin
cases.risk: A naive startsWith check lets verify.itisyou.app.attacker.example pass as same-origin
cases.setup: Origin values 'https://verify.itisyou.app.attacker.example' and 'https://verify.itisyou.app'
cases.expected: Only the exact origin is accepted

cases.requirement: The CSRF cookie is issued with the __Host- prefix and without a Domain attribute
cases.risk: A Domain-scoped CSRF cookie can be overwritten by a sibling subdomain, which defeats the double-submit pattern entirely
cases.setup: csrfCookie output inspected for attributes
cases.expected: The cookie name is __Host-verify_csrf and the header carries no Domain attribute

cases.requirement: A magic-link token is single-use: the second redemption is refused
cases.risk: A link sitting in an inbox or a mail-scanner log would otherwise remain a live credential indefinitely
cases.setup: A signin token redeemed once successfully then presented again
cases.expected: The second attempt is refused, consumed_at remains the first redemption time, and no second session is created

cases.requirement: An expired magic-link token is refused even if never consumed
cases.risk: A long-lived login link is a credential with no revocation; the expiry is the only bound on it
cases.setup: A signin token whose expires_at has passed
cases.expected: Redemption is refused with a plain-language message and no session is created

cases.requirement: Magic-link tokens are stored as hashes, so the login_tokens table holds no usable credential
cases.risk: The same breach argument as sessions, at the point where a stolen row grants a fresh login rather than an existing one
cases.setup: A token issued and the login_tokens row inspected
cases.expected: token_hash is a hash and the plaintext token appears in no column

cases.requirement: Repeated failed redemptions of one token increment attempts and eventually lock that token
cases.risk: Without a per-token attempt bound, a short token space could be brute-forced from the link endpoint
cases.setup: Ten failed redemption attempts against one token hash prefix
cases.expected: attempts increments and further attempts are refused regardless of correctness

cases.requirement: Requesting a magic link for an unknown email returns the same response as for a known one
cases.risk: A differing response turns the login form into an account-enumeration oracle against our whole customer list
cases.setup: Link requests for a registered address and an unregistered one
cases.expected: Both responses are identical in status, body and timing band, and only the registered address receives an email

cases.requirement: A magic-link request is rate limited per email and per source bucket
cases.risk: Unbounded requests let an attacker flood a customer's inbox and burn our Resend sending allowance
cases.setup: Six link requests for one address inside the rate-limit window
cases.expected: Later requests return 429 with a retry-after and send no further email

cases.requirement: A token issued with purpose 'invite' cannot be redeemed at the signin endpoint
cases.risk: Purpose confusion lets an invitation for a viewer role be redeemed as a full sign-in for a different account
cases.setup: An invite-purpose token presented to the signin redemption route
cases.expected: The redemption is refused and no session is created

cases.requirement: A token issued with purpose 'owner_bootstrap' cannot create a platform owner once an owner already exists
cases.risk: A second platform owner created from a leftover bootstrap token is a total compromise of the operations panel
cases.setup: An owner_bootstrap token redeemed while a user with is_platform_owner 1 already exists
cases.expected: The redemption is refused and no additional owner is created

cases.requirement: A revoked session is rejected on its next request
cases.risk: Revocation that only takes effect at expiry means a customer who signs out on a shared machine is still signed in
cases.setup: A session with revoked_at set, used on an authenticated route
cases.expected: The request is treated as anonymous and redirected to sign-in

cases.requirement: An expired session is rejected even though its row still exists
cases.risk: Sessions outliving their expiry make the expiry a comment rather than a control
cases.setup: A session whose expires_at has passed, used on an authenticated route
cases.expected: The request is treated as anonymous

cases.requirement: Signing out revokes the server-side session rather than only clearing the cookie
cases.risk: A cookie-only sign-out leaves a live session that anyone holding the captured cookie can keep using
cases.setup: A sign-out request followed by a replay of the original cookie
cases.expected: The replayed cookie is rejected and the sessions row carries revoked_at

cases.requirement: Signing out of one session does not revoke the user's other sessions
cases.risk: Silently ending a customer's other devices is a usability failure that looks like a security incident
cases.setup: A user with two sessions where one signs out
cases.expected: The other session continues to work and retains its revoked_at as null

cases.requirement: last_seen_at is updated on use without extending expires_at past its issued lifetime
cases.risk: A sliding expiry with no absolute cap turns a session into a permanent credential
cases.setup: A session used repeatedly across its lifetime
cases.expected: last_seen_at advances while expires_at remains the originally issued absolute value

cases.requirement: A session for a disabled user is rejected
cases.risk: Disabling an account must take effect immediately, not when the last session happens to expire
cases.setup: A user with disabled_at set holding a live session
cases.expected: The request is treated as anonymous and the session is revoked on detection

cases.requirement: A session marked is_automation cannot perform a state-changing customer action
cases.risk: Automation identities exist to exercise the product; letting one mutate real data makes every test run a production write
cases.setup: An is_automation session POSTing to a workflow update route in a non-synthetic workspace
cases.expected: The request is refused with 403 and no row is modified

cases.requirement: An is_automation session is confined to workspaces marked is_synthetic
cases.risk: A test identity that can read a real customer's runs is a cross-tenant leak created by our own tooling
cases.setup: An is_automation session reading runs in a workspace with is_synthetic 0
cases.expected: The read returns nothing and the attempt is recorded in audit_events

cases.requirement: An invitation token is single-use and its redemption creates exactly one membership
cases.risk: A reusable invitation lets a forwarded email add unlimited people to a paying customer's workspace
cases.setup: An invitation redeemed once then presented again
cases.expected: One memberships row exists, redeemed_at is set, and the second attempt is refused

cases.requirement: An invitation redeemed by an email other than intended_email is refused
cases.risk: Otherwise a forwarded invitation grants access to whoever opens it first
cases.setup: An invitation for ann@example.com redeemed while signed in as bob@example.com
cases.expected: The redemption is refused and no membership is created

cases.requirement: An expired invitation is refused
cases.risk: An invitation with no effective expiry is a standing grant on a customer's data
cases.setup: An invitation whose expires_at has passed
cases.expected: Redemption is refused with a plain-language expiry message

cases.requirement: An invitation grants exactly the role it was issued with and cannot be escalated at redemption
cases.risk: A viewer invitation redeemed as an admin would hand over billing and connection control
cases.setup: A workspace_viewer invitation redeemed with an admin role parameter in the request body
cases.expected: The created membership has role workspace_viewer and the supplied parameter is ignored

cases.requirement: An invitation cannot be created for a workspace the inviter does not administer
cases.risk: Otherwise any authenticated user could invite themselves into any workspace by id
cases.setup: A workspace_admin of workspace A creating an invitation naming workspace B
cases.expected: The request is refused with 403 and no invitations row is created for workspace B

cases.requirement: A workspace_viewer cannot create an invitation
cases.risk: Viewers are the least-trusted role; letting them add members defeats the point of the role
cases.setup: A viewer session POSTing to the invitation route
cases.expected: The request is refused with 403

cases.requirement: Revoking an unredeemed invitation prevents its later redemption
cases.risk: An invitation sent in error must be recallable, or the only remedy is deleting the workspace
cases.setup: An invitation revoked before redemption then presented
cases.expected: Redemption is refused and no membership is created

cases.requirement: The plan's seat limit is enforced: a second viewer invitation is refused
cases.risk: The published plan is one owner plus one invited viewer; unlimited seats gives away the product's only capacity dimension
cases.setup: A workspace already holding one admin and one viewer creating a second viewer invitation
cases.expected: The request is refused with 422 naming the seat limit

cases.requirement: An anonymous request to any /app route is redirected to sign-in and never renders customer data
cases.risk: An unauthenticated read of a dashboard is the most basic breach a web product can have
cases.setup: Unauthenticated GETs across every /app route
cases.expected: Every route responds with a redirect to sign-in and no response body contains workspace data

cases.requirement: An anonymous POST to any state-changing route is refused before any handler logic runs
cases.risk: A write path that checks authentication late can have already had a side effect by the time it refuses
cases.setup: Unauthenticated POSTs across every state-changing route
cases.expected: Every route responds 401 or a redirect and no database row is created or modified

cases.requirement: A workspace_viewer can read runs and reports but cannot modify workflow rules
cases.risk: The viewer role is what a customer gives their own client; a viewer who can edit rules can change what is being verified
cases.setup: A viewer session reading a run report and then PUTting workflow rules
cases.expected: The read succeeds and the write is refused with 403 leaving the workflow version unchanged

cases.requirement: A workspace_viewer cannot reach billing or open the Stripe portal
cases.risk: A viewer with billing access can cancel a subscription they do not pay for
cases.setup: A viewer session requesting the billing page and the portal-session route
cases.expected: Both are refused with 403 and no Stripe call is made

cases.requirement: A workspace_viewer cannot create, rotate or read a workflow signing key
cases.risk: The signing key authorises event submission; a viewer holding it can inject events into the customer's verification record
cases.setup: A viewer session on the signing-key routes
cases.expected: All are refused with 403 and no credential version is created

cases.requirement: A workspace_admin cannot reach any /owner route
cases.risk: The owner panel dispatches tests, approves spending and runs cleanup across all tenants
cases.setup: A workspace_admin session requesting each /owner route
cases.expected: Every route responds 404 or 403 without revealing that the panel exists

cases.requirement: A platform_owner has no implicit read access to a customer workspace's evidence
cases.risk: Operational access to customer evidence must be a deliberate, audited act rather than a property of the owner role
cases.setup: A platform_owner session reading a customer workspace's evidence endpoint with no explicit grant
cases.expected: The read is refused and the attempt is recorded in audit_events

cases.requirement: Role is resolved server-side from the session and a role field in the request body is ignored
cases.risk: Engineering rule 5 exists because a browser-supplied role is the simplest possible privilege escalation
cases.setup: A viewer session POSTing a body containing role 'workspace_admin'
cases.expected: The request is authorised as a viewer and refused

cases.requirement: workspace_id is resolved server-side from the session's membership and never taken from the request
cases.risk: A browser-supplied workspace id is a direct cross-tenant read if any handler trusts it
cases.setup: An authenticated request carrying a workspace_id parameter for a workspace the user does not belong to
cases.expected: The handler uses the session's workspace and returns nothing for the supplied one

cases.requirement: A user with memberships in two workspaces sees only the active workspace's runs
cases.risk: Mixing two workspaces' runs in one list is a cross-tenant leak to a legitimate but wrong audience
cases.setup: A user in workspaces A and B reading the run list while A is active
cases.expected: Only workspace A's runs are returned

cases.requirement: Requesting a run by an id belonging to another workspace returns not-found rather than forbidden
cases.risk: A distinguishable forbidden response confirms the id exists, which turns a scoping check into an enumeration oracle
cases.setup: Workspace B requesting a run id owned by workspace A
cases.expected: The response is 404 with the same body shape as a genuinely unknown id

cases.requirement: Evidence for a run is readable only within the run's own workspace
cases.risk: Evidence carries the most sensitive data we hold; a scoping miss here is the worst version of a tenancy bug
cases.setup: Workspace B requesting the evidence endpoint for workspace A's run
cases.expected: The response is 404 and no evidence content appears in the body

cases.requirement: An export contains only the requesting workspace's data
cases.risk: An export is a file the customer keeps and may forward; foreign rows in it are a leak that outlives the request
cases.setup: An export generated for workspace A in a database populated for A and B
cases.expected: Every row in the export carries workspace A's identifiers and no B identifier appears

cases.requirement: An export is authorised for workspace_admin only and refused for a viewer
cases.risk: A bulk export is the highest-volume read in the product; the least-trusted role should not be able to take one
cases.setup: A viewer session requesting an export
cases.expected: The request is refused with 403 and no export artefact is generated

cases.requirement: A deletion request removes only the requesting workspace's data
cases.risk: An over-reaching deletion destroys another paying customer's records with no recovery path
cases.setup: A deletion executed for workspace A alongside a populated workspace B
cases.expected: Workspace A's rows are removed and every workspace B row count is unchanged

cases.requirement: An owner action requires recent strong authentication recorded in mfa_verified_at
cases.risk: A stolen owner session cookie would otherwise be enough to approve spending and dispatch jobs across the whole platform
cases.setup: A platform_owner session with mfa_verified_at null attempting an owner action
cases.expected: The action is refused and the owner is sent to the TOTP step

cases.requirement: An owner session whose mfa_verified_at is older than the strong-auth window must re-verify
cases.risk: An indefinite MFA grant makes the second factor a one-time formality rather than a control
cases.setup: A platform_owner session whose mfa_verified_at is beyond the configured window
cases.expected: The owner action is refused pending re-verification while ordinary reads continue to work

cases.requirement: A replayed TOTP code is refused within its own validity window
cases.risk: A code captured from a shoulder-surfed screen or a shared terminal is otherwise usable for the rest of its period
cases.setup: The same TOTP code submitted twice inside one time step
cases.expected: The first submission succeeds and the second is refused

cases.requirement: TOTP verification tolerates a bounded clock skew and refuses a code outside it
cases.risk: Too little tolerance locks the owner out of their own platform; too much widens the replay window
cases.setup: Codes generated one step early, on time, one step late and three steps late
cases.expected: The first three are accepted and the fourth is refused

cases.requirement: The owner's TOTP secret is stored only as a credential_versions reference, never in the users row
cases.risk: A secret in the users table is exposed by any user-level read, including a support query or a backup
cases.setup: An enrolled owner's users row inspected
cases.expected: totp_secret_ref holds a reference and no column contains the secret material

cases.requirement: A failed owner sign-in attempt is recorded in audit_events with no credential material
cases.risk: Without an audit trail an attack on the owner account is invisible; with credential material in it the audit log becomes the target
cases.setup: Three failed owner authentications
cases.expected: Three audit_events rows exist with actor_kind 'user' and no code, secret or cookie value in redacted_metadata

cases.requirement: A customer can sign in with a magic link and reach their dashboard
cases.risk: This is the first thing every paying customer does; if it is broken nothing else in the product can be reached
cases.setup: A seeded user requesting a link, with the link captured from the stubbed mail transport
cases.expected: Following the link lands on the dashboard showing that workspace's name

cases.requirement: Signing out returns the customer to the public site and the back button does not restore the dashboard
cases.risk: A dashboard restored from the browser cache after sign-out exposes data on a shared machine
cases.setup: A signed-in customer signing out then navigating back
cases.expected: The back navigation shows the sign-in page and no cached workspace data

cases.requirement: A viewer sees the run report without any edit, billing or connection controls
cases.risk: Controls a viewer cannot use are either a broken promise when they work or a dead end when they do not
cases.setup: A viewer session on the dashboard, workflow and report pages
cases.expected: No edit, billing or connection action is rendered anywhere in those pages

cases.requirement: A form submitted without its CSRF token is refused and the page explains what happened
cases.risk: A bare 403 on a form submission reads as a product fault and generates support contacts
cases.setup: A workflow rules form submitted with the CSRF field stripped
cases.expected: The submission is refused and the page shows a plain-language message with a way to retry

cases.requirement: The owner panel is unreachable for a signed-in customer and leaks no hint that it exists
cases.risk: A discoverable admin surface invites targeted attack on a single-operator product
cases.setup: A workspace_admin session navigating directly to the owner panel URL
cases.expected: The response is a not-found page with no owner-specific wording, link or asset

cases.requirement: The owner reaches the panel only after completing the second factor
cases.risk: The panel controls spending and platform-wide jobs; a single-factor route into it is the highest-value target in the system
cases.setup: A platform_owner signing in with a magic link and navigating to the panel
cases.expected: The panel is withheld until the TOTP step is completed, then renders

cases.requirement: money() refuses a non-integer amount
cases.risk: A fractional pence entering the system is how a cap silently drifts and a charge stops reconciling
cases.setup: money(29.5) and money(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 1)
cases.expected: Both throw TypeError and no Money value is produced

cases.requirement: addMoney and subtractMoney refuse a currency mismatch rather than coercing
cases.risk: Adding pounds to euros produces a number that looks plausible and is wrong by a factor nobody notices until reconciliation
cases.setup: addMoney(money(100,'GBP'), money(100,'EUR'))
cases.expected: The call throws TypeError naming the currency mismatch

cases.requirement: formatMoney renders LIMITS.PLAN_PRICE_PENCE as £29.00
cases.risk: The price is a public commercial claim; a rendering error here is a pricing error on the marketing page
cases.setup: formatMoney(money(LIMITS.PLAN_PRICE_PENCE))
cases.expected: The output is exactly '£29.00'

cases.requirement: formatMoney renders a sub-pound amount and a negative amount without losing the leading zero or the sign
cases.risk: A credit rendered as £5.0 or £5.00 instead of -£5.00 is a customer-visible billing error
cases.setup: formatMoney for 5 pence and for -500 pence
cases.expected: The outputs are '£0.05' and '-£5.00'

cases.requirement: budgetAvailableMinor subtracts spent, reserved, committed and the safety buffer
cases.risk: A missing term in this formula is the difference between staying inside the founder's authorised budget and exceeding it
cases.setup: A BudgetAccountState with all five fields populated
cases.expected: The returned value equals limit minus the four deductions, computed only in integers

cases.requirement: canReserve refuses a negative or non-integer request
cases.risk: A negative reservation would increase available budget, which is a spending authorisation created out of arithmetic
cases.setup: canReserve called with -100 and with 10.5
cases.expected: Both return false and neither mutates the account state

cases.requirement: Boundary: canReserve accepts a request exactly equal to the available amount and refuses one penny more
cases.risk: The cap is only real at its boundary; an off-by-one here spends money nobody authorised
cases.setup: An account with 500 available, requests of 500 and 501
cases.expected: 500 returns true and 501 returns false

cases.requirement: An order may move from checkout_created to payment_pending to active
cases.risk: This is the happy path every paying customer takes; a missing edge blocks all revenue
cases.setup: The order state machine driven through the successful sequence
cases.expected: Each transition is accepted and the terminal state is active

cases.requirement: An order cannot move from active back to draft or checkout_created
cases.risk: Reopening a paid order is how a customer ends up with two subscriptions for one workspace
cases.setup: Transitions attempted from active to draft and to checkout_created
cases.expected: Both are refused with a typed error and the order stays active

cases.requirement: An order cannot move from cancelled or refunded to active
cases.risk: A resurrected cancelled order restores service that was paid for and then returned
cases.setup: Transitions attempted from cancelled to active and from refunded to active
cases.expected: Both are refused and the order state is unchanged

cases.requirement: An order rejected for plan incompatibility records a rejection_reason and never reaches checkout
cases.risk: Sending an incompatible customer to a payment page takes money for something we cannot deliver
cases.setup: An order evaluated as incompatible by the plan compatibility check
cases.expected: The order state is rejected, rejection_reason is populated, and no checkout session is created

cases.requirement: An expired checkout session moves the order to expired rather than leaving it payment_pending forever
cases.risk: Orders stuck at payment_pending block the customer from starting a new checkout
cases.setup: A checkout session past its expiry with no completion event
cases.expected: The order state becomes expired and a new checkout may be created

cases.requirement: The checkout amount and price id are taken from server-side configuration, never from the request
cases.risk: A browser-supplied price is the classic e-commerce tampering attack and would let anyone buy the plan for a penny
cases.setup: A checkout creation request whose body contains amount_minor 1 and a foreign price id
cases.expected: The created session uses LIMITS.PLAN_PRICE_PENCE and the configured price id; the supplied values are ignored

cases.requirement: A checkout session is created against the Stripe mode configured for the environment
cases.risk: A live-mode session created from staging charges a real card during a test
cases.setup: Checkout creation in an environment configured as test mode
cases.expected: The Stripe call is made in test mode and the billing_customers row records environment 'test'

cases.requirement: A workspace that already holds an active subscription cannot start a second checkout
cases.risk: Two active subscriptions for one workspace is a double charge and an immediate refund and a support case
cases.setup: Checkout creation for a workspace whose subscriptions row is active
cases.expected: The request is refused with 409 and no Stripe call is made

cases.requirement: A workspace_viewer cannot create a checkout session
cases.risk: Anyone who can start a checkout can commit the workspace owner to a recurring charge
cases.setup: A viewer session POSTing to the checkout route
cases.expected: The request is refused with 403 and no orders row is created

cases.requirement: The billing_customers row binds one Stripe customer per workspace per environment
cases.risk: Two Stripe customers for one workspace splits the billing history and makes reconciliation impossible
cases.setup: Two checkout creations for one workspace in the same environment
cases.expected: One billing_customers row exists and both orders reference the same stripe_customer_id

cases.requirement: Card details never reach the application: no request body or log line carries a PAN or CVC
cases.risk: Hosted Checkout exists precisely so we never hold card data; a single log line with it changes our compliance obligations entirely
cases.setup: The full checkout path exercised with a recording logger and request capture
cases.expected: No captured request body or log record contains a card number, expiry or CVC field

cases.requirement: A Stripe webhook with an invalid signature is rejected and has no effect
cases.risk: Unsigned webhook acceptance means anyone can grant themselves a paid subscription with a single POST
cases.setup: A checkout.session.completed payload with a corrupted signature header
cases.expected: The response is 400, no subscriptions row is created and the receipt is recorded as invalid

cases.requirement: A Stripe webhook whose timestamp is outside STRIPE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS is rejected
cases.risk: A captured webhook replayed later could reactivate a cancelled subscription
cases.setup: A correctly signed payload timestamped ten minutes ago
cases.expected: The response is 400 and no subscription state changes

cases.requirement: Stripe signature verification runs against the raw request bytes
cases.risk: Verifying a re-serialised body accepts any semantically equivalent payload and defeats the signature
cases.setup: A payload whose byte representation differs from the signed one but parses identically
cases.expected: Verification fails and the webhook is rejected

cases.requirement: A duplicate Stripe event id is processed exactly once
cases.risk: Stripe retries aggressively; a second effect means a second entitlement grant or a second refund
cases.setup: The same checkout.session.completed event delivered four times
cases.expected: One subscriptions row exists, one entitlements row is granted, and later deliveries are recorded as duplicate

cases.requirement: An out-of-order subscription event does not overwrite newer state
cases.risk: Stripe does not guarantee ordering; a stale past_due arriving after active locks a paying customer out of their own product
cases.setup: customer.subscription.updated with created 200 (status active) processed, then created 100 (status past_due)
cases.expected: The subscriptions row remains active and provider_event_created stays at 200

cases.requirement: Subscription status is written only from a verified provider event, never from a browser request
cases.risk: Engineering rule 5: a browser-settable subscription status is free service for anyone who reads our HTML
cases.setup: An authenticated POST attempting to set subscriptions.status to active
cases.expected: No such route accepts the field and the row is unchanged

cases.requirement: An event for a subscription belonging to another environment is ignored
cases.risk: Test-mode events applied to live data grant free service; live events applied to test data corrupt the test environment
cases.setup: A test-mode subscription event delivered to the production handler
cases.expected: The event is recorded as ignored and no live subscriptions row changes

cases.requirement: An event for an unknown Stripe customer is recorded and ignored rather than attributed by guesswork
cases.risk: Guessing the workspace for an unattributable payment event grants a paid plan to the wrong customer
cases.setup: A subscription event whose customer id matches no billing_customers row
cases.expected: The receipt records processing_status 'ignored', no entitlement is granted, and the owner queue shows the orphan

cases.requirement: A successful checkout grants an entitlement with run_limit LIMITS.PLAN_RUNS_PER_PERIOD
cases.risk: The allowance is the product's only capacity dimension; granting the wrong number either loses revenue or oversells
cases.setup: A verified checkout.session.completed event for a new workspace
cases.expected: An entitlements row exists for the current billing period with run_limit 500 and consumed 0

cases.requirement: A renewal for the next billing period creates a new entitlements row rather than resetting the old one
cases.risk: Overwriting the old row destroys the usage record the customer may dispute a charge against
cases.setup: invoice.paid for the following period on an active subscription
cases.expected: A second entitlements row exists for the new period and the previous period's consumed value is preserved

cases.requirement: A past_due subscription enters the grace policy: existing runs still resolve but new events are refused
cases.risk: Cutting off resolution of in-flight runs punishes a customer for a card expiry and destroys evidence they have already paid for
cases.setup: A workspace moved to past_due with two PENDING runs and a new event submission
cases.expected: The two PENDING runs continue to be observed and resolve; the new submission is refused with a billing message

cases.requirement: Boundary: the grace period ends at its configured length and further resolution stops
cases.risk: An unbounded grace period is free service; a grace period that ends early is an angry customer with a failed card
cases.setup: A workspace at past_due observed one second before and one second after the grace boundary
cases.expected: Resolution continues before the boundary and stops after it, with the same plain-language reason shown

cases.requirement: A canceled subscription refuses new events immediately while leaving historical reports readable
cases.risk: Deleting a former customer's history at cancellation destroys records they may need and invites a chargeback
cases.setup: A workspace whose subscription is canceled, submitting an event and reading its run history
cases.expected: The submission is refused and the history renders in full

cases.requirement: An unpaid subscription is treated as not entitled, not as active
cases.risk: Treating unpaid as active is unbilled service that accrues silently until someone reads the Stripe dashboard
cases.setup: A workspace whose subscriptions row is unpaid submitting an event
cases.expected: The submission is refused and the entitlement check reports the workspace as not entitled

cases.requirement: A trialing subscription is entitled and consumes allowance normally
cases.risk: Trials that do not consume allowance make the trial a free unlimited plan
cases.setup: A workspace in trialing status submitting five events
cases.expected: All five are accepted and consumed reaches 5

cases.requirement: Entitlement is resolved server-side from the subscription, never from a request field
cases.risk: A request-supplied entitlement is free unlimited service for anyone who can send a POST
cases.setup: An event submission whose body contains entitlement and run_limit fields
cases.expected: The supplied fields are ignored and the entitlement is read from the subscriptions row

cases.requirement: Cancellation at period end keeps service until current_period_end and stops after it
cases.risk: Cutting service off at the cancellation click takes payment for time not served
cases.setup: A subscription with cancel_at_period_end 1, submitting events before and after current_period_end
cases.expected: Submissions before the period end are accepted and those after are refused

cases.requirement: A refund request is recorded as 'requested' and never submitted to Stripe without owner approval
cases.risk: Automatic refunds are money leaving the business on an unapproved trigger
cases.setup: A customer-initiated refund request
cases.expected: A refunds row exists in state 'requested' or 'queued_for_owner' and no Stripe refund call is made

cases.requirement: An owner-approved refund is submitted once and the approval is consumed
cases.risk: A reusable approval is an unbounded authorisation to move money
cases.setup: An approval granted for one refund, with the refund submitted and the approval re-presented
cases.expected: The refund is submitted once, the approval status becomes 'consumed', and the second use is refused

cases.requirement: A refund exceeding the approval's maximum_amount_minor is refused
cases.risk: An approval that does not bind the amount is an open cheque
cases.setup: An approval for 2900 pence used to submit a refund of 5800 pence
cases.expected: The submission is refused, the refunds row stays unsubmitted and the attempt is audited

cases.requirement: A refund whose canonical payload differs from the approved hash is refused
cases.risk: Binding only the action type lets an approved refund be redirected to a different order or customer
cases.setup: An approval hashed over order A used to submit a refund for order B
cases.expected: The submission is refused with a mismatch error and no Stripe call is made

cases.requirement: A retried refund submission with the same idempotency key does not create a second Stripe refund
cases.risk: A double refund cannot be reversed without asking the customer to pay again
cases.setup: Two submissions of the same refund after a timeout on the first
cases.expected: One Stripe refund is created and both calls return the same provider_refund_id

cases.requirement: A refund that Stripe reports as failed moves to 'failed' and does not silently retry
cases.risk: A silent retry loop on a failed refund can eventually succeed several times
cases.setup: A Stripe refund response with a failure status
cases.expected: The refunds row state becomes 'failed', the reason is recorded, and the owner queue shows it for manual action

cases.requirement: A succeeded refund cancels the entitlement for the refunded period
cases.risk: Refunding the money while leaving the service running gives the product away
cases.setup: A refund succeeding for the current period's payment
cases.expected: The entitlements row for that period is marked not entitled and new submissions are refused

cases.requirement: A refund cannot be requested for an order belonging to another workspace
cases.risk: Cross-tenant refund requests would let one customer trigger money movement on another's account
cases.setup: Workspace B requesting a refund naming workspace A's order id
cases.expected: The request is refused with 404 and no refunds row is created

cases.requirement: Reconciliation flags a local subscription with no matching provider record
cases.risk: A local row with no provider counterpart is service given away with no payment behind it
cases.setup: A subscriptions row whose provider id is absent from the stubbed provider listing
cases.expected: The reconciliation report lists the row as unmatched and it is surfaced in the owner queue

cases.requirement: Reconciliation flags a provider subscription with no local row
cases.risk: A payment taken with no local entitlement is a customer paying for nothing, which becomes a chargeback
cases.setup: A stubbed provider listing containing a subscription absent locally
cases.expected: The reconciliation report lists it as missing locally and does not create the row automatically

cases.requirement: Reconciliation flags a status divergence rather than overwriting local state automatically
cases.risk: Blind overwriting during reconciliation can cancel an active customer from a stale provider page
cases.setup: A local row showing active where the provider reports canceled
cases.expected: The divergence is reported for owner decision and the local row is unchanged until acted on

cases.requirement: Reconciliation records reconciled_at without altering matched rows
cases.risk: Touching matched rows makes it impossible to tell a real update from a reconciliation pass in the audit trail
cases.setup: A reconciliation pass over rows that all match
cases.expected: Only reconciled_at changes on those rows

cases.requirement: Reconciliation never runs against live Stripe from a test or staging environment
cases.risk: A staging reconciliation reading live subscriptions is a cross-environment data path that could cancel real customers
cases.setup: Reconciliation invoked with ENVIRONMENT staging and STRIPE_MODE test
cases.expected: Only test-mode records are read and any live-mode call is refused

cases.requirement: The pricing page shows £29 read from LIMITS.PLAN_PRICE_PENCE rather than a hard-coded string
cases.risk: A price on the page that disagrees with the price charged is a consumer-law problem, not just a bug
cases.setup: The public pricing page rendered and compared against the constant
cases.expected: The rendered price matches formatMoney(money(LIMITS.PLAN_PRICE_PENCE))

cases.requirement: A customer who abandons Stripe Checkout returns to the app with no subscription and a clear next step
cases.risk: A dead end after abandoning checkout loses a customer who was one click from paying
cases.setup: A checkout started then cancelled at the Stripe-hosted page, returning via the cancel URL
cases.expected: The app shows the plan page with no subscription claimed and an obvious way to try again

cases.requirement: The billing page shows the current period's run usage against the 500 allowance
cases.risk: A customer who cannot see their usage discovers the limit only when their automation starts being refused
cases.setup: Seeded workspace with consumed 312 in the current period
cases.expected: The billing page shows 312 of 500 runs used for the named period

cases.requirement: A customer approaching the allowance sees a warning before they hit it, not after
cases.risk: Silent exhaustion means the customer's enquiries stop being verified with no notice, which is the failure mode they bought us to prevent
cases.setup: Seeded workspace at 460 of 500 runs consumed
cases.expected: The dashboard shows a usage warning naming the remaining runs and what happens at the limit

cases.requirement: Cancelling through the Stripe Billing Portal is reflected in the app without the browser asserting it
cases.risk: The app must learn about cancellation from Stripe, not from the page the customer was returned to
cases.setup: A cancellation performed in a stubbed portal followed by the corresponding webhook
cases.expected: The app shows cancel_at_period_end and the service-end date only after the webhook is processed

cases.requirement: No content string contains a forbidden guarantee word such as guaranteed, certified or 100% uptime
cases.risk: These claims are explicitly forbidden and are the kind of wording that turns a marketing page into a legal exposure
cases.setup: Every exported string in packages/ui/src/content scanned against the forbidden-wording list
cases.expected: No string matches any forbidden term in any language or casing variant on the list

cases.requirement: No content string claims real-time or instant verification
cases.risk: Results depend on a one-minute cron and a deadline of up to an hour; the claim would be false on the product's own schedule
cases.setup: Content scanned for 'real-time', 'realtime' and 'instant'
cases.expected: No such claim appears in home, pricing, faq or legal content

cases.requirement: No content string claims support for a CRM or email provider other than HubSpot and Resend
cases.risk: Claiming 'any CRM' sells a product that cannot be delivered and generates immediate refunds
cases.setup: Content scanned for connector claims against the built connector list
cases.expected: Only HubSpot and Resend are named as supported evidence sources

cases.requirement: The pricing content reads its price and allowance from LIMITS rather than repeating a literal
cases.risk: A literal in content is how the page and the charge diverge without anyone noticing
cases.setup: Static inspection of the pricing content module
cases.expected: The module references LIMITS.PLAN_PRICE_PENCE and LIMITS.PLAN_RUNS_PER_PERIOD and hard-codes neither

cases.requirement: The coverage-mode caveat is present in the public content and is not phrased as a footnote
cases.risk: The scope document requires this as a standing caveat; burying it is how a negative claim quietly disappears
cases.setup: The home and FAQ content inspected for the missing-run caveat
cases.expected: The caveat appears in the body copy of both, stating that a run that never started is undetectable in customer_triggered mode

cases.requirement: The 'accepted' versus 'delivered' distinction is preserved wherever email evidence is described
cases.risk: Merging the two words in copy makes a public claim the evidence cannot support
cases.setup: All content strings mentioning email outcomes
cases.expected: Each describes acceptance and delivery separately and never uses one word for the other

cases.requirement: A new signup creates exactly one workspace with the user as workspace_admin
cases.risk: A signup that creates two workspaces or the wrong role blocks the customer at their first action
cases.setup: A completed signup for a new email address
cases.expected: One workspaces row and one memberships row with role workspace_admin exist

cases.requirement: Public signup can never create a platform_owner
cases.risk: A self-service route to the owner role is total platform compromise
cases.setup: A signup whose request body sets is_platform_owner and role fields
cases.expected: The created user has is_platform_owner 0 and the supplied fields are ignored

cases.requirement: The onboarding checklist reports the real state of each step rather than a stored flag
cases.risk: A checklist that ticks a step the system has not actually completed sends the customer to their first run with a broken setup
cases.setup: A workspace with HubSpot ready, Resend expired, rules saved and no payment
cases.expected: The checklist shows connections partially complete, rules complete and payment outstanding, derived from the live rows

cases.requirement: Saving invalid workflow rules returns 422 with the failing field and does not create a workflow version
cases.risk: A silently rejected rule change leaves the customer verifying against rules they think they replaced
cases.setup: A rules save with an assertion whose operator and expected type disagree
cases.expected: The response is 422 naming the assertion and no workflow_versions row is created

cases.requirement: Editing rules creates a new workflow version and leaves past runs bound to their original version
cases.risk: Rewriting history means a customer's evidence report no longer matches what was actually checked at the time
cases.setup: A workflow with one completed run whose rules are then edited
cases.expected: A second workflow_versions row exists and the completed run still references version 1

cases.requirement: A workflow cannot be activated without at least one mandatory assertion
cases.risk: An all-optional workflow would report VERIFIED for everything, which is worse than no monitoring
cases.setup: An activation attempt on a workflow whose assertions are all optional
cases.expected: Activation is refused with 422 and the workflow stays in draft

cases.requirement: The demo workflow runs entirely on synthetic data and touches no provider
cases.risk: A demo that calls a real provider spends quota and could expose another account's data to a prospect
cases.setup: The demo route exercised with a fetch stub that fails on any call
cases.expected: The demo completes, its workspace is marked is_synthetic, and no outbound call is attempted

cases.requirement: Demo data is never mixed into a real workspace's run history or usage counters
cases.risk: Demo runs counted against a paid allowance would be a billing error the customer can see
cases.setup: A demo run executed while the user also holds a real workspace
cases.expected: The demo run belongs to the synthetic workspace and the real workspace's consumed value is unchanged

cases.requirement: The proof run on the setup page uses the customer's real rules against seeded synthetic evidence
cases.risk: A proof run against different rules proves nothing about the configuration the customer is about to rely on
cases.setup: A setup proof run for a workspace with three assertions
cases.expected: The proof run evaluates all three of the customer's assertions and is recorded as synthetic

cases.requirement: A support case stores a redacted body and never the raw submission
cases.risk: Customers paste API keys, record ids and full email threads into support forms without thinking
cases.setup: A support submission whose body contains an email address and a token-shaped string
cases.expected: The stored body_redacted has both masked and the raw text is stored nowhere

cases.requirement: A support case submitted by an anonymous visitor is accepted with no workspace_id
cases.risk: The security policy directs vulnerability reports to this form; requiring an account would close that route
cases.setup: An anonymous support submission in the security category
cases.expected: A support_cases row exists with workspace_id null and priority set from the category

cases.requirement: Support submissions are rate limited per contact email
cases.risk: An unbounded form is a spam vector into the owner's only support queue
cases.setup: Eight submissions from one address inside the window
cases.expected: Later submissions return 429 and create no further rows

cases.requirement: A support case linked to a run is only linkable to a run in the submitter's own workspace
cases.risk: A linked run id from another workspace would put a foreign run's context into someone else's support thread
cases.setup: A submission from workspace B naming a run id owned by workspace A
cases.expected: The case is created with linked_run_id null and the mismatch is recorded

cases.requirement: An export is produced as a file the customer can download, containing runs, assertions and redacted evidence summaries
cases.risk: The evidence artefact is the thing an agency shows their own client; an export missing it is not worth taking
cases.setup: An export requested for a workspace with twelve runs
cases.expected: The export contains all twelve runs with their assertions and redacted evidence summaries

cases.requirement: Every CSV field in an export is neutralised against spreadsheet formula injection
cases.risk: A field beginning with = or + executes in the customer's spreadsheet the moment they open our file
cases.setup: An export where a CRM property value is '=HYPERLINK("http://x","click")'
cases.expected: The exported field is prefixed so the spreadsheet treats it as text

cases.requirement: An export contains no unmasked credential, token or full email address
cases.risk: An export is the largest single egress of customer data in the product and it leaves our control entirely
cases.setup: An export from a workspace whose evidence carried recipient addresses and whose connection holds credentials
cases.expected: No credential appears and every address is masked by the redaction helper

cases.requirement: A deletion request removes customer data and leaves an audit record that the deletion happened
cases.risk: Deleting the record of the deletion makes the commitment unprovable to the customer who asked for it
cases.setup: A completed deletion for one workspace
cases.expected: No customer-scoped rows remain and an audit_events row records the deletion with no customer content in it

cases.requirement: Deletion revokes sessions and retires credentials rather than only removing rows
cases.risk: A live session or an unretired provider credential after deletion is continued access to something that should be gone
cases.setup: A deletion for a workspace with two live sessions and two ready connections
cases.expected: All sessions are revoked, all credential_versions carry retired_at, and no further provider call is possible

cases.requirement: Deletion is refused while a subscription is still active, with a clear instruction to cancel first
cases.risk: Deleting under an active subscription leaves a customer being charged for data that no longer exists
cases.setup: A deletion request from a workspace with an active subscription
cases.expected: The request is refused with a message naming cancellation as the required first step

cases.requirement: The home page states what the product does and what it deliberately does not do, above the fold on a narrow viewport
cases.risk: The negative claims are the product's credibility; putting them where nobody reads them is the same as not making them
cases.setup: The home page at a 375px-wide viewport
cases.expected: Both the capability statement and at least one explicit limitation are visible without scrolling past the first screen

cases.requirement: The public site renders and is navigable with JavaScript disabled
cases.risk: The architecture is server-rendered Hono JSX with progressive enhancement; a JS-dependent nav would contradict the stack decision and exclude locked-down corporate browsers
cases.setup: Home, pricing, FAQ and support pages loaded with scripting disabled
cases.expected: Every page renders its content and every primary navigation link works

cases.requirement: The demo runs from the public site without an account and shows all four statuses
cases.risk: A prospect who cannot see an UNVERIFIED result will not understand the product's central distinction before they buy
cases.setup: The public demo exercised end to end as an anonymous visitor
cases.expected: The demo produces and explains a VERIFIED, a FAILED, an UNVERIFIED and a PENDING result

cases.requirement: The demo is labelled as synthetic data everywhere it appears
cases.risk: An unlabelled demo that looks like live data is a misleading claim about the service's current state
cases.setup: Every demo view and its printable output
cases.expected: Each carries a visible synthetic-data label

cases.requirement: Pricing, FAQ and legal pages are reachable from every public page
cases.risk: A pricing page nobody can find is a conversion failure; unreachable legal pages are a compliance failure
cases.setup: Link graph traversal from each public page
cases.expected: Every public page links to pricing, FAQ and the legal pages

cases.requirement: A new customer can complete signup, connect both providers and save rules in one sitting
cases.risk: This is the whole activation path; a break anywhere in it means no customer ever reaches their first run
cases.setup: A fresh signup driven through connection authorisation with stubbed providers and a rules save
cases.expected: The checklist ends fully complete and the workflow is ready to activate

cases.requirement: The setup page explains the correlation property requirement in plain language before asking for it
cases.risk: This is the one setup step that requires real work in the customer's own CRM and is where activation dies silently
cases.setup: The rules step of onboarding
cases.expected: The page explains what a correlation property is, why it is needed and what to do if their automation does not write one

cases.requirement: A customer can copy their signing key exactly once and is told it will not be shown again
cases.risk: A key the customer loses with no warning means rebuilding their automation integration from scratch
cases.setup: The signing key step after key generation
cases.expected: The key is shown once with an explicit warning and is not retrievable from any later page

cases.requirement: Rotating the signing key warns that in-flight submissions signed with the old key will be refused
cases.risk: A silent rotation breaks the customer's live automation at the moment they feel most confident
cases.setup: The key rotation action on the settings page
cases.expected: A confirmation step states the consequence before the rotation is applied

cases.requirement: A workspace with no runs shows an empty state that explains the next action and claims no success rate
cases.risk: '100% success' with zero runs is the specific dishonesty the README promises to avoid
cases.setup: A newly activated workspace with zero runs viewed on the dashboard
cases.expected: The dashboard shows an empty state with a next action and displays no percentage

cases.requirement: A workspace whose connection has expired shows the problem on the dashboard, not only on the connections page
cases.risk: A customer who does not visit the connections page will see only a wall of unverified runs and blame the product
cases.setup: A workspace with an expired HubSpot connection and four UNVERIFIED runs
cases.expected: The dashboard shows the connection problem as the cause with a direct link to reconnect

cases.requirement: The dashboard distinguishes PENDING from UNVERIFIED in wording and in styling
cases.risk: These are the two states customers confuse, and confusing them turns an in-flight run into a perceived failure
cases.setup: A dashboard showing one PENDING and one UNVERIFIED run
cases.expected: The two are labelled differently, styled differently and each carries its own explanation

cases.requirement: A server error on the dashboard shows a recoverable error state with a request id and no stack trace
cases.risk: A raw error page leaks internals and leaves the customer with nothing to quote to support
cases.setup: The dashboard route forced to throw
cases.expected: The page shows a plain-language error with a request id and no stack, file path or internal identifier

cases.requirement: The dashboard remains usable at 320px width with no horizontal scrolling of the page body
cases.risk: Agencies check client status from a phone; a dashboard that needs sideways scrolling is not usable in that moment
cases.setup: The dashboard at a 320px viewport
cases.expected: No horizontal page scroll is present and every primary action is reachable

cases.requirement: Primary navigation is reachable and operable on a narrow viewport without a pointer
cases.risk: A mobile menu that only works by tap excludes keyboard and switch-access users from the whole application
cases.setup: Navigation opened and traversed by keyboard at a 375px viewport
cases.expected: The menu opens, every item is reachable by keyboard and focus is trapped and restored correctly

cases.requirement: A FAILED report names the specific rule that was contradicted and what was observed instead
cases.risk: A failure with no specifics sends the customer hunting through their automation with no lead
cases.setup: A run whose mandatory email delivery assertion was contradicted by a bounce
cases.expected: The report names the rule, shows expected and observed values and gives the plain-language reason

cases.requirement: An UNVERIFIED report states explicitly that this is not a failure of the customer's automation
cases.risk: The whole product depends on customers trusting this distinction rather than reading unverified as broken
cases.setup: A run that resolved UNVERIFIED because the CRM connection was unavailable
cases.expected: The report states it is not a failure, names the access problem and gives the action that would resolve it

cases.requirement: A report is printable to a single readable page for sharing with the agency's own client
cases.risk: The report is the artefact that settles a dispute; if it cannot be shown to a third party it has no commercial value
cases.setup: A VERIFIED report rendered in print styling
cases.expected: The printed output contains the verdict, the rules, the evidence references and the coverage-mode caveat on one page

cases.requirement: A run list filtered to failures shows only failures and says so in the heading
cases.risk: A filtered list that reads like the full list makes a customer think everything failed
cases.setup: A run list filtered to FAILED in a workspace with mixed results
cases.expected: Only failed runs are listed and the heading names the active filter

cases.requirement: A customer can submit a support request from inside the app with their workspace context attached
cases.risk: Support with no context costs a round trip on every case, which a single-operator business cannot absorb
cases.setup: A support submission from an authenticated session
cases.expected: The created case carries the workspace id and the customer sees a confirmation with a reference

cases.requirement: A customer can request an export and a deletion from the account page and is told what each does
cases.risk: A deletion the customer did not fully understand is an irreversible loss they will hold us responsible for
cases.setup: The account page export and deletion actions
cases.expected: Each explains its scope and consequences, and deletion requires an explicit typed confirmation

cases.requirement: Cancellation explains exactly what happens to data and to in-flight runs before it is confirmed
cases.risk: A customer who cancels without understanding data retention will ask for an emergency restore we cannot provide
cases.setup: The cancellation flow up to its confirmation step
cases.expected: The confirmation states the service-end date, what happens to history and what happens to runs still pending

cases.requirement: The canonical payload serialiser orders object keys deterministically
cases.risk: An approval hash that depends on key order can be evaded by reordering the same JSON, which makes every approval meaningless
cases.setup: stableStringify over two objects with identical entries in different key orders
cases.expected: Both produce the same string and therefore the same hash

cases.requirement: The canonical serialiser distinguishes the string '1' from the number 1
cases.risk: Type coercion in the canonical form lets a payload of a different type reuse an approval intended for another
cases.setup: stableStringify over {amount:1} and {amount:'1'}
cases.expected: The two outputs differ

cases.requirement: The canonical serialiser rejects a payload containing a function, symbol or circular reference
cases.risk: An unserialisable payload that silently degrades to a partial string would produce an approval bound to less than the caller intended
cases.setup: stableStringify over a circular object and an object holding a function
cases.expected: Both throw rather than producing a partial canonical form

cases.requirement: An approval binds to the exact canonical payload hash and refuses any other payload
cases.risk: An approval that binds only to an action type is an open authorisation to perform that action on anything
cases.setup: An approval granted for payload A, presented with payload B of the same action type
cases.expected: Consumption is refused with a mismatch error and the approval remains 'granted'

cases.requirement: An approval binds to a single action_type and cannot be used for a different one
cases.risk: Cross-action reuse would let an approval for a cleanup preview authorise a campaign submission
cases.setup: An approval for action_type 'refund.submit' presented for 'campaign.submit'
cases.expected: Consumption is refused

cases.requirement: An approval carries a maximum_amount_minor that bounds every monetary use of it
cases.risk: An unbounded money approval is the single most dangerous object in the system
cases.setup: An approval with maximum_amount_minor 2900 used for an action costing 5800
cases.expected: Consumption is refused with the amount named in the error

cases.requirement: An approval is single-use: consumption moves it to 'consumed' and a second attempt is refused
cases.risk: A reusable approval turns one authorisation into unlimited spending
cases.setup: An approval consumed once and presented again
cases.expected: The second attempt is refused and the status remains 'consumed'

cases.requirement: An expired approval is refused even if never consumed
cases.risk: An approval with no effective expiry is a standing authorisation the owner has forgotten about
cases.setup: An approval whose expires_at has passed
cases.expected: Consumption is refused and the status becomes 'expired'

cases.requirement: A revoked approval is refused
cases.risk: An approval granted in error must be withdrawable before it is used
cases.setup: An approval revoked then presented for consumption
cases.expected: Consumption is refused and no action is performed

cases.requirement: Approval consumption and the action it authorises commit atomically
cases.risk: A consumed approval with no action means the owner must re-approve; an action with an unconsumed approval means the approval can be used again
cases.setup: A refund submission interrupted between the approval update and the action write
cases.expected: Either both are present or neither is, with no intermediate state visible

cases.requirement: A concurrent double consumption of one approval results in exactly one action
cases.risk: Two simultaneous clicks on an approve button must not produce two refunds
cases.setup: Two concurrent consumptions of one granted approval
cases.expected: One succeeds, the other is refused, and one action record exists

cases.requirement: Every approval grant and consumption is recorded in audit_events with the payload hash and no payload content
cases.risk: The audit trail is how the founder reconstructs what was authorised; embedding the payload would put customer data into the audit log
cases.setup: An approval granted then consumed
cases.expected: Two audit_events rows exist carrying the action type and hash and no payload body

cases.requirement: An approval cannot be granted by anyone other than a platform_owner with recent strong authentication
cases.risk: The approval mechanism is the platform's only spending control; anything short of owner plus second factor makes it decorative
cases.setup: Approval grant attempted by a workspace_admin and by an owner with stale mfa_verified_at
cases.expected: Both are refused with 403 and no approvals row is created

cases.requirement: A quality run dedupe_key prevents the same suite and commit being queued twice
cases.risk: Duplicate quality runs waste the runner's time and produce two contradictory result rows for one commit
cases.setup: Two queue requests for the same suite and commit sha
cases.expected: One quality_runs row exists and the second request returns the existing run

cases.requirement: A quality run records total, passed, failed and skipped counts from the report rather than from the request
cases.risk: Self-reported counts from the requester are how a green gate is faked
cases.setup: A completed run whose request body claims 500 passed and whose report shows 480 passed and 20 failed
cases.expected: The stored counts come from the report and the request's claimed numbers are ignored

cases.requirement: A quality run with any failure can never be recorded as 'passed'
cases.risk: A gate that can be marked green with failures in it is worse than no gate
cases.setup: A report with 499 passed and 1 failed
cases.expected: The run state is 'failed' and the failing case id is retained in the report reference

cases.requirement: A quality run that reports skipped cases records them and does not count them as passed
cases.risk: Counting skips as passes is the most common way a 500-case count becomes a fiction
cases.setup: A report with 480 passed, 0 failed and 20 skipped
cases.expected: The stored counts distinguish the 20 skips and the displayed total does not fold them into passed

cases.requirement: A quality run's limitations field records what the suite did not prove
cases.risk: The honesty section of the test plan is only real if it is attached to each run's result
cases.setup: A completed run whose suite used only mocked providers
cases.expected: The limitations field states that providers were mocked and that no real integration was exercised

cases.requirement: A quality run that loses its runner mid-execution ends as infrastructure_error, not failed
cases.risk: Recording an infrastructure loss as a product failure sends the owner hunting a bug that does not exist
cases.setup: A running quality run whose runner stops sending heartbeats past the timeout
cases.expected: The run state becomes infrastructure_error with the reason recorded

cases.requirement: A cancelled quality run is distinguishable from a failed one in both state and display
cases.risk: Conflating a deliberate cancellation with a failure corrupts the record the launch gate is read from
cases.setup: A queued run cancelled by the owner
cases.expected: The run state is 'cancelled' and it is excluded from pass and fail counts

cases.requirement: A runner device pairs only with a valid, unexpired pairing code and becomes active
cases.risk: An unpaired or loosely paired runner is an unauthenticated executor of typed jobs on the owner's behalf
cases.setup: A pairing attempt with a valid code and another with an expired one
cases.expected: The valid attempt moves the device to 'active'; the expired one is refused and the device stays pending_pair

cases.requirement: A pairing code is stored as a hash and is single-use
cases.risk: A reusable pairing code left in a chat log pairs an attacker's machine as a trusted runner
cases.setup: A pairing code used once then presented again
cases.expected: pairing_code_hash holds a hash, the second use is refused, and no second device is activated

cases.requirement: A revoked runner device cannot lease or complete a job
cases.risk: A revoked device that can still finish work means revocation does not actually revoke anything
cases.setup: A revoked device attempting to lease a queued job and to post a result for a job it already held
cases.expected: Both are refused and the job returns to the queue

cases.requirement: A job lease is bound to a device id and a nonce, so another device cannot post its result
cases.risk: Without the binding, any paired device could claim credit for or corrupt another device's job result
cases.setup: Device B posting a result for a job leased by device A
cases.expected: The post is refused and the job's result_json is unchanged

cases.requirement: An expired job lease returns the job to the queue rather than stranding it
cases.risk: A stranded job blocks the owner's only maintenance channel with no visible cause
cases.setup: A leased job whose lease_expires_at has passed with no result
cases.expected: The job state returns to 'queued' and a different device may lease it

cases.requirement: A maintenance job is typed: an unrecognised typed_kind is refused at enqueue
cases.risk: An untyped or free-form job is arbitrary code execution on the owner's machine dressed as a feature
cases.setup: An enqueue request with typed_kind 'shell'
cases.expected: The request is refused with 422 and no maintenance_jobs row is created

cases.requirement: A maintenance job payload is validated against its typed schema before it reaches a runner
cases.risk: Validating on the runner means a malformed payload has already crossed the trust boundary
cases.setup: An enqueue for a known typed_kind with a payload missing a required field
cases.expected: The request is refused with 422 and nothing is queued

cases.requirement: A maintenance job that spends money requires a bound approval before it can be leased
cases.risk: A job that can spend without approval bypasses the entire budget control
cases.setup: A spending-class job queued with no approval_id and leased
cases.expected: The lease is refused and the job stays awaiting_runner with the missing approval named

cases.requirement: A job result is recorded once; a second post for the same job is refused
cases.risk: Duplicate results would overwrite the record the owner acts on and could mark a failed job passed
cases.setup: Two result posts for one leased job
cases.expected: The first is recorded and the second is refused with the existing state returned

cases.requirement: A runner heartbeat updates last_heartbeat_at without extending any job lease
